nodes.NAME: qeunconm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Capital output ratio for unconventional energy multiplier.  A multiplier on all types of energy capital output, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the amount of capital required per unit of energy output and lower values decrease it. Lower this parameter gradually over time to simulate a decreased cost of an energy form (such as renewable energy) as a result of technological advance.  Raise it over time to simulate the addition to the capital cost of an energy form (say nuclear) as a result of the addition to those costs of environmental ones.

nodes.NAME: QEUNCON(Oil)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Capital output ratio for unconventional energy, in dollars, per barrel of production capacity, by region and energy category.  This variable determines how many dollars of capital are required in the production of a barrel of oil equivalent in each energy category.  It therefore represents the cost of energy production.  QEUNCON is exogenous only for nuclear and renewable energy.  Values for oil, gas, and coal are computed endogenously (and depend on remaining resources) and should be examined only as indicators.  To change the cost pattern for those energy forms, use resorm and increase or decrease resources.  Values for renewable and nuclear energy can be exogenously changed, but you should maintain the initial value of the base case.  A series of gradually lower costs could represent technological progress (e.g. in the solar component of renewable).  A series of gradually higher costs could represent the impact of environmental factors (e.g. increasing costs of nuclear waste disposal).  Higher or lower values will increase or decrease investment in a particular energy category and will affect its production level.  You should be aware that investment will respond only to changes over time in QE and not to changes in the initial condition.

nodes.NAME: resorunconm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Ultimately recoverable unconventional resource multiplier, by energy type.  This parameter allows the user to increase or decrease ultimately recoverable resource values.  A value of 1 accepts the values of RESOR as specified.  A value of 1.5 would raise the resource levels for a specific energy form in a specific country/region by 50 percent.  This multiplier is unusual in that it is only important in the first year - it should not be changed over time because after ultimate resources are calculated the first year they can only run down (be used up).

nodes.NAME: resoruncon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Resources of unconventional fossil fuels, ultimate, billion barrels of oil equivalent.  This value only sets an initial condition; thereafter resources are computed taking into account depletion from production.

nodes.NAME: etechadvuncon

Use, for example, to decrease the cost of renewable energy over time.  A value of 0.01 applied to renewable energy would force an annual decrease in the costs of producing solar energy of 1% each year, representing continued technological advance in such production (a value of -0.01 would represent a negative cost decrease, that is, a cost increase).

nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the start age to apply Longevity Logistic Curve

nodes.NAME: ictintnethhm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Percentage of households with Internet access, multiplier to change the percentage exogenously

nodes.NAME: ictcomputersm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Percentage of households with a Personal Computer, multiplier to change the percentage exogenously

nodes.NAME: aidlpm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Aid, loan portio multiplier.  This multiplier interacts with the coefficient that determines the portion of foreign aid that actually constitutes loans.

nodes.NAME: npowf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Nuclear power factor, warheads/billion $ expenditure.

nodes.NAME: infrateledtfp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for fixed telephone network divestment  time, number of years from peak. Peak is at 30% of mobile phone access.

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingceiling
nodes.Parameter Explanation: User can specify maximum smoking prevalence, Impacts countries rising through stage 2 (risking to peak).

nodes.NAME: infraroadraisetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of Standard Errors to be targeted by the forecast (between -2 and 2), 0 turns off the targetting.

nodes.NAME: infraroadraiseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of years to target a given number of Standard Errors by the forecast.

nodes.NAME: ally
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Alliance membership switch.  A value of 1 indicates membership in the acting alliance and a value of 2 indicates membership in the reacting alliance (either alliance can consist of a single country or region).  Alliances can form or dissolve over time; membership in alliances can change.  None of that will, however, happen endogenously; you must specify alliance structures.  Alliance membership only affects war damage, not threat levels or war outbreak.

nodes.NAME: edsecupprgradgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, upper secondary (general), Graduation rate to the last grade, annual additive growth. A parameter to make the countries meet education targets by an annual additive growth in the survival rate in general upper secondary.

nodes.NAME: mhw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Import propensity, historical (inertial) delay in change.  Values near 1.0 imply very rapid adjustment and values near 0 imply little or no adjustment.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: survseadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive factor to introduce a shift in Survival/self-expression index for a region/country.  It increases or decreases the index value that the model calculates.  The normal value is zero.  See also and contrast with cultshmp, which is a cultural shift for the large cultural regions identified in the WVS project and which is calculated from data.

nodes.NAME: tradsratadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive factor to introduce a shift in Traditional/rational-secular indexindex for a region/country.  It increases or decreases the index value that the model calculates.  The normal value is zero.  See also and contrast with cultshmp, which is a cultural shift for the large cultural regions identified in the WVS project and which is calculated from data.

nodes.NAME: igdpr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Initial GDP growth rate, expressed in decimal form.  A value of 0.03 is equal to a rate of 3%.  Only changes in this parameter for the very first year of the model run will affect model behavior.

nodes.NAME: LAPOPR
nodes.Parameter Explanation: No longer used as parameter.  Now a computed variable.

nodes.NAME: LD(Crop)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Land in million hectares, by region and land category.  You can change this initial condition to represent different assumptions about land availability for agriculture.  Only initial values can be changed; the model subsequently computes land by category endogenously.

nodes.NAME: LD(Grazing)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Land in million hectares, by region and land category.  You can change this initial condition to represent different assumptions about land availability for agriculture.  Only initial values can be changed; the model subsequently computes land by category endogenously.

nodes.NAME: LD(Forest)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Land in million hectares, by region and land category.  You can change this initial condition to represent different assumptions about land availability for agriculture.  Only initial values can be changed; the model subsequently computes land by category endogenously.

nodes.NAME: LD(Other)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Land in million hectares, by region and land category.  You can change this initial condition to represent different assumptions about land availability for agriculture.  Only initial values can be changed; the model subsequently computes land by category endogenously.

nodes.NAME: LD(Urban)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Land in million hectares, by region and land category.  You can change this initial condition to represent different assumptions about land availability for agriculture.  Only initial values can be changed; the model subsequently computes land by category endogenously.

nodes.NAME: govbuscostm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the cost of starting a business.

nodes.NAME: govbusregindm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the level of government regulation of Business Index.

nodes.NAME: ICTCONSURPLUS
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Consumer-captured surpluses from cost reductions and capability enhancements as the technologies develop (i.e., surpluses not represented in standard economic measures such as gross domestic product)

nodes.NAME: labinformcoeffed
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is used to change the coefficient of education years (15+ years, both sexes)  in the multiple regression of informal labor shares.

nodes.NAME: armsimmaxpctmilexp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Share of GDS(MIL) cap on MARMS

nodes.NAME: marriedfemshrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for the share of female who are in a marriage or a union. Values greater than 1 raises the share relative to the base case value for the same year. Values lower than 1 lowers the share.

nodes.NAME: marriageedseclowr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Responsiveness of lower secondary graduation rate of girls to changes in the share of girls married. A value of .5 means a increase in the graduation rate by half a percentage point for a 1 percent reduction in the share of girls who are in a marriage.

nodes.NAME: marriageedsecuppr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Responsiveness of upper secondary graduation rate of girls to changes in the share of girls married. A value of .5 means a increase in the graduation rate by half a percentage point for a 1 percent reeducation in the share of girls who are in a marriage.

nodes.NAME: ageofmarriagem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The rate of change for age of marriage impacted by a multliplier.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: labfemshrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on share of females in the total labor force.

nodes.NAME: ldwf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Incremental land used for residential, transportation and industrial purposes, in hectares per capita of population.  It quantifies the transition of land associated with net population changes between urban and other land types like crop, grazing, or forest areas.

nodes.NAME: democwvlen
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the democracy wave length in years (peak to trough/half-wave).  Historical waves of democracy have been variable in length, so it is very reasonable to speculate that they could change from the base value or over time.

nodes.NAME: elgrevdebt2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of government revenues to changes in government debt levels.  Elprst1 and elprst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: labretagem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on labor force retirement age. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year

nodes.NAME: HTCGRI
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Government Response to Trafficking Index

nodes.NAME: HTCTPI
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Human Trafficking Prevalence Index

nodes.NAME: gdsbudgetprotec
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is for budget protection. (1 = full protection, 0 is no protection) Values in between 0 and 1 indicates the share of demanded budget that will be set aside of the normalization process.

nodes.NAME: gdstrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that sets the target valye of GDS target, as a share of GDP. Used in combination with gdstrgtyr.

nodes.NAME: gdstrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that sets the number of years to reach the GDS target, set by gdstrgtval.

nodes.NAME: govconswing
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter brings in convergence between development function determined spending and demand side (bottom-up) calculation of spending.

nodes.NAME: gdsbudgetconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter brings in convergence between development function determined spending and demand side (bottom-up) calculation of spending.

nodes.NAME: aidgradpoint
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on aid received..  The model will allocate available aid so that all recipients receive aid proportional to specified targets, not necessarily equal to those targets.

nodes.NAME: landirareaactualm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on land area actually irrigated.

nodes.NAME: HLSTUNTWORK
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The percentage of the population in working age that is affected by childhood malnutrition

nodes.NAME: bilateraltradeforwardlinksw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to compute forward linkages from bilateral trade.

nodes.NAME: xfdiwgrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Global Foreign Direct Investment.

nodes.NAME: watprid
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Responsiveness of water price to change in stock/inventory levels.

nodes.NAME: watprii
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Responsiveness of water price to stock/inventory levels.  watprii and watprid are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities), most of which normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: wastewatertreatedm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on treated waster water.

nodes.NAME: waterrenewconverge
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the time for country to return to exploitable limit of renewable freshwater resources.

nodes.NAME: watertoyieldswitch
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to allow water to constrain agricultural yields.

nodes.NAME: aitaskm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Artificial Inteligence Index for Specific Tasks.

nodes.NAME: aimachiqm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Artificial Inteligence Machine IQ.

nodes.NAME: agxm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on agricultural exports, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase investment and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: enmm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on energy imports, by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase imports and lower values decrease them.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: enxm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on energy exports, by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase exports and lower values decrease them.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: msm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on import, by sector and region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase imports and lower values decrease them.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: xsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on exports by sector and region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase exports and lower values decrease them.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: mbasehw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Import base, historical (inertial) delay in change.  Values near 1.0 imply complete historical inertia and values near 0 very rapid adjustment.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: xcadjsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for export capacity adjustment. When the switch is ON, we adjust Exports based on changes in imports from main partners.

nodes.NAME: labparm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on labor participation rate. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value.

nodes.NAME: xworkremitinm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Worker Remittances Received.

nodes.NAME: xworkremitoutm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Worker Remittances Sent.

nodes.NAME: tfpshockadjshr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: In economic shock such as COVID period, the proportion of change to GDP that has persistent impact on TFP (TEFF); rest of affect goes to temporary capacity utilization.

nodes.NAME: malnpoppsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for malnourished population. A value of 1 indicates that the effect is on and uses full distribution, while a value of 0 indicates off (as in the base case).

nodes.NAME: diploembassym
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Standarized Number of Embassies that a country can have in other countries in a given year

nodes.NAME: igdprcor
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Initial GDP corrected growth rate, expressed in decimal form.  A value of 0.03 is equal to a rate of 3%.  Only changes in this parameter for the very first year of the model run will affect model behavior.

nodes.NAME: ken
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Capital for energy, in billion dollars, by region and energy category.  This variable determines how many billion dollars of capital are required in total in each energy category.  It therefore represents the cost of energy production.

nodes.NAME: wppowhhsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, power index switch, 1 means using POWERHH index to drive forward linkages, instead of the defaul POWER index.

nodes.NAME: povagesexagratnat
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch that determines the ratio of age-group poverty to national poverty. A value of 0 merges the ratio to a target level, i.e., the average of high income countries while any other value sets it to the multiple of initial.

nodes.NAME: agmvaluem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Billion $ Value of agricultural imports, by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase imports and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: agxvaluem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Billion $ Value of agricultural exports, by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase exports and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: xfdiwgradd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive Factor on Global Foreign Direct Investment.

nodes.NAME: xportwgrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Portfolio Investment World Growth.

nodes.NAME: numnwplim
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter sets the limit on the number of networked persons, expressed in decimal terms. For example,  a value of .85 would introduce an assumption that networking will ultimately saturate at 85% of the population (some people will be too young or will not be networked for other reasons).

nodes.NAME: infmorttfrlag
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines rate of change in moving average of infant mortality in the Total Fertility Rate equation. A value of 0 indicates no lag, 1 indicates no change and 0.9 indicates a long lag.

nodes.NAME: hlexpcostgaptohealthel
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter  that controls link between expenditures-cost gap and health outcomes.

nodes.NAME: hlcostleyrper
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Cost of the Life Extension intervension for the SENS project in Thousand $ per year person

nodes.NAME: hlcostletime
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Duration of the Life Extension intervension for the SENS project in years, meaning that people need to take the treatment again after this amount of years

nodes.NAME: HLCOSTLESUB
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The subsidy that low income countries received for getting the life extension treatment, based on GDPPC relationship with the US in the base year

nodes.NAME: hlcostotherrattarget
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the ratio of cost (other) to the sum of mortality, morbidity and life extension cost as a target to forecast other cost.

nodes.NAME: infraelecacctrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal access in electrification.

nodes.NAME: landarablepot
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Potentially arable land represents the maximum crop land value for each country.

nodes.NAME: labunemprm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on labor unemployment rate. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value.

nodes.NAME: hlmortconstsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for mortality constant. A value of 1 indicates it is on, while a value of 0 indicates off.

nodes.NAME: hlstuntchlsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch that activates relationship between child stunting and communicable diseases. This relationship is used in the Health module to affect Communicable Diseases (Diarrhea, Respiratory Infections and Other CDs) when Child Stunting level changes from the expected value.

nodes.NAME: infraelecacctrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the value of percentage access considered as universal access to electrification.

nodes.NAME: ictbroadtrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal access to fixed broadband

nodes.NAME: hllongvtybeta
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Beta coeficient that controls the shape of the mortality function (higher values make it steep, 0 makes it flat at 0, 1 makes it flat at 1).

nodes.NAME: hllongvtyalphaconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence parameter that controls how fast (in how many years) the Alpha coeficient reaches its target.

nodes.NAME: diplodistancetoeu
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The physical distance between a country and Europe (Belgium)

nodes.NAME: DIPLOEMBASSY
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Standarized Number of Embassies that a country has in other countries in a given year

nodes.NAME: DIPLOEMBASSYMAX
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Standarized Maximum Number of Embassies that a country can have in other countries in a given year

nodes.NAME: diploembassymaxm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Standarized Maximum Number of Embassies that a country can have in other countries in a given year

nodes.NAME: DIPLOIGO
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Standarized Weighted Number of Intergovernmental Organizations that a country belongs in a given year

nodes.NAME: DIPLOIGOMAX
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Standarized Maximum Weighted Number of Intergovernmental Organizations that a country can belong in a given year

nodes.NAME: diploigomaxm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Standarized Maximum Weighted Number of Intergovernmental Organizations that a country can belong in a given year

nodes.NAME: DIPLOTREATY
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Standarized Weighted Number of Treaties that a country has signed (1) or ratified (2) in a given year

nodes.NAME: DIPLOTREATYMAX
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Standarized Maximum Weighted Number of Treaties that a country can sign (1) or ratify (2) in a given year

nodes.NAME: diplotreatymaxm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier Standarized Maximum Weighted Number of Treaties that a country can sign (1) or ratify (2) in a given year

nodes.NAME: hltfragehalflife
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the number of years after which the total fertility halves.

nodes.NAME: hltfragestop
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the age of menopause to stop the total fertility distribution.

nodes.NAME: hltfrageinit
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the initial age to start fertility distribution.

nodes.NAME: hltfragepeak
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the peak age of fertility distribution.

nodes.NAME: hltfrpeaklevel
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the peak level for fertility distribution

nodes.NAME: hlmorbconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines/controls the convergence time of Morbidity vector reaching its target.

nodes.NAME: hhsaveneedrat
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Allows the user to create an initial discrepancy between accumulated savings (HHSAVSTOCK) and integrated need (HHSAVNEEDSTOCK).

nodes.NAME: climeconimpsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to turn on the impacts of temperature rise on non-agricultural sectors.

nodes.NAME: climeconimplin
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameteter on linear term in the quadratic function that links changes in temperature to impact on economy in percentage terms.

nodes.NAME: climeconimpsq
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameteter on squared term in the quadratic function that links changes in temperature to impact on economy in percentage terms.

nodes.NAME: histgdpforce
nodes.Parameter Explanation: GDP forcing switch, historic runs only.  A value of 1  turns on the use of historic data for GDP in an historical run.  A value of 0 turns it off.

nodes.NAME: ictbroadurimpmax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal access to fixed broadband

nodes.NAME: ictbroadurimpmin
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal access to fixed broadband

nodes.NAME: gdsnormalize
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for government finance model normalizatio. The base value of 1 normalizes all GDS to GOVCON, while a value of 0 allocates whatever is demanded by GDS and GOVCON does not get affected.

nodes.NAME: infrapubspndflr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure Finance. Minimum pulic spending on infrastructure as a % of GDP. Sum of infrastructure and infraother will be close to this.

nodes.NAME: infrapubspndflrsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, public spending, minimum, switch between flat and function

nodes.NAME: ensolfueltrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to eliminate solid fuel use

nodes.NAME: mfpinfrte
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is currently inactive.

nodes.NAME: hlsmkel
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter controls the shorter term impact of smoking rate on smoking.

nodes.NAME: hlsmkimeff
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter controls the shorter term impact of smoking rate on smoking.

nodes.NAME: gemm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the Gender Empowerment Measure (GEM).

nodes.NAME: govnucwpadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Adds to or subtracts from the number of nuclear weapons countries have

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingtcs
nodes.Parameter Explanation: TCS is the weighted average of the list of 6 specific areas in which countries should work to reduce smoking, according to the tobacco control treaty.

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingtcsel
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of TCS with smoking rates.

nodes.NAME: govriskm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government risk, and this affects governance security index and government quality index.

nodes.NAME: govsecrskdiv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: User can specify the divisor of the government peformance risk value to security. Higher values lower the contribution, and vice-versa.

nodes.NAME: govsecrskexp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: User can specify the contribution of the government peformance risk value to security. Higher values lower the contribution, and vice-versa.

nodes.NAME: hltfrconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence parameter that controls how fast (in how many years) the Mortality Vector reaches its target

nodes.NAME: hlmorbm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on initial morbidity to set a target for morbidity.  value of -1 is used as a switch to turn off the multiplier, otherwise used as a multiplier on initial morbidity.

nodes.NAME: retireconsumrat
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Allows the user to control the spending in retirement relative to average spending at all ages.

nodes.NAME: savingsdiscountrt
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Discount rate used to compute working age  and savings rate needed with changes in Life Expectancy.

nodes.NAME: globalfundsrecipients
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for global fund recipients. A value of 1 indicates on; 0 indicates off.

nodes.NAME: ldcropunusedshare
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the unused share of cropland.

nodes.NAME: ENVTEMP
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The average annual temperature by country/region

nodes.NAME: envtemptoginidomsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to turn on temperature to Gini Index impacts. A value of 0 indicates off; 1 sets it to U-shaped; 2 to elasticity; 3 to incremental U-shaped; 4 to absolute elasticity; 5 to Paglialunga and 6 to Paglialunga with average temperature.

nodes.NAME: envtemptoginidomel
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Gini Index to changes in temperature.

nodes.NAME: workageretiresv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Age of retirement to compute savings rate, input for function to compute Savings rate needed, it allows to analyze Savings rate needed independently of changes in retirement age when using mixed scenarios.

nodes.NAME: wpextinterv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: External intervention forcing switch.  A value of 1 turns on the intervention in a country from another country (unspecified); it will affect internal conflict

nodes.NAME: ENVYLCHG
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The annual change in agricultural yield by country/region

nodes.NAME: envclimsens
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that defines time sensitivity of how global temperatures change with the level of CO2 emissions.

nodes.NAME: trucksconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence time for truck sales in years. This value determines the number of years over which all countries/regions will converge to the chosen function (as determined by the switch, vehfuncsw) for the computation of truck sales per year.  A value of 1000 would effectively turn off convergence, so that initial country-specific variations from the function would be maintained over time.  A value of 60 would lead to near convergence by the middle of the 21st century.  Very rapid convergence seems improbable in the face of fundamental country differences in infrastructure, land area, culture, etc.

nodes.NAME: gdpinformcoeffintercept
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is used to change the intercept of the multiple regression of informal GDP shares.

nodes.NAME: gdpinformcoeffrand
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is used to change the coefficient of R & D spending (total, as a % of GDP)  in the multiple regression of informal GDP shares.

nodes.NAME: gdpinformcoefflabinf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is used to change the coefficient of Informal Labor Share  in the multiple regression of informal GDP shares.

nodes.NAME: gdpinformcoeffcorrupt
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is used to change the coefficient of Corruption Index  in the multiple regression of informal GDP shares.

nodes.NAME: infinformcoeffintercept
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter can be used to change the intercept of the regression of informal employment in informal enterprises.

nodes.NAME: hlmortcdadltm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on communicable disease mortality for adults aged between 15 to 49.

nodes.NAME: wpcon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, change in dispute threat with power concentration.  This value is used in a function as a multiplier on global power concentration among great powers (PCONGREAT), a variable which itself normally ranges from approximately 0.2 to 0.4.  The change in the result of the product from year to year provides an additive term that can be interpreted as an additive increase (or decrease) in the probability of disputes between two countries/regions.

nodes.NAME: wpconsq
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, change in dispute threat with the square of change in power concentration (see also wpcon).  This value is used in a function as a multiplier on the square of global power concentration among great powers (PCONGREAT), a variable which itself normally ranges from approximately 0.2 to 0.4.  The change in the result of the product of the parameter and the square of concentration from year to year provides an additive term that can be interpreted as an additive increase (or decrease) in the probability of disputes between two countries/regions.

nodes.NAME: wpthrwar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, portion of all disputes that escalate to wars.  The value is in percent. Thus 3.3 would indicate that the probability of a war between two states would be 3.3% if they experienced a militarized international dispute (or 0.33% if the probability of a dispute were 10%).  This parameter is not now being use to generate wars from disputes.

nodes.NAME: eltfrcon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of total fertility rate to contraception use.  For most model users, it is much easier to directly manipulate fertility (see tfrm).

nodes.NAME: elascd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of crop food demand to prices.  Values (normally negative) near 0 imply little responsiveness of demand to prices and larger absolute values (near -1) imply considerable responsiveness.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elasde
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy demand with price change, by region.  This value should be negative and normally will not change much over time.  Significant changes in the value from specification in the base case could lead to difficulties or instability in energy market clearing (balancing of supply and demand).

nodes.NAME: elasdi
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy discoveries to prices.  This value should be positive and normally will not change much over time.  Significant changes in the value from specification in the base case could lead to difficulties or instability in energy markets.

nodes.NAME: elashc
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of mortality to health care expenditures.

nodes.NAME: waterhhcostlowershr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, water services, share of services using lower-cost service. Base case value is 50/50 when both lower and upper cost services are available

nodes.NAME: hlwatsansw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the effect on diarrheal diseases when access to water and sanitation changes from the expected values.

nodes.NAME: climeconimpstk
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the share of production function (technology and/or climate stock) that climate change to economic impact variable eliminates. For example, CLIMECONIMP of 2 percent times 0.5 will indicate a 1 percent reduction of stock in capital/technology.

nodes.NAME: labcoeffsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on technology coefficients by sector and skill level.

nodes.NAME: labdemsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on labor demand, by country/region, sector and skill.

nodes.NAME: migrateinm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Inward migration of a population in percent per year.  Because global emigration and immigration must balance, changes in this value for a single country/region may not change migration/population as substantially as the change introduced originally.

nodes.NAME: migrateoutm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Migration rate multiplier outward.  A multiplier on migration rate , unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase mortality and lower values decrease it.

nodes.NAME: migratesw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to replace migration in our population module using dyadic formulation

nodes.NAME: ictbroadmobiltrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal access to mobile broadband

nodes.NAME: goveffectsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the target standard errors for GOVEFFECT forecast. Value range between -2 to 2, with 0 indicating that the target is turned off. Used in combination with goveffectseyrtar.

nodes.NAME: gemseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies that number of years to reach the standard error target for GEM.

nodes.NAME: govdebtchg
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that represents an additive factor for Government debt change as % of GDP. It can represent relief by debt holders or expenditures in crisis with no net addition to recipient finances.  A value of 0 implies no net debt change by exogenous assumption.

nodes.NAME: hdigdppcmaxun
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the maximum GDP per capita, used for calculation of  HDI component. Users will normally not change this parameter.

nodes.NAME: minpcgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameters is used to adjust the impact of population of growh on initialization of economic growth (IGDPR), it adds to POPR/100 for the limit of IGDPR

nodes.NAME: govcorruptseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies that number of years to reach the standard error target for GOVCORRUPT.

nodes.NAME: hlmlnsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter activates linkages between malnutrition and communicable diseases. It is used in the health module to affect communicable diseases when malnutrition changes from expected values. A value of 1 indicates on; 0 indicates off.

nodes.NAME: edpricostadjrural
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A multiplier to adjust the marginal unit cost (per student expenditure) of primary education expanding to rural areas

nodes.NAME: edprigndreqintn
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education primary, no of years (from firstyear) by which gender parity in net primary intake rate is reached. The gender parity index is the ratio of the male rate to the female rate. Must set edgndreqintnon=1 for this to work.

nodes.NAME: elxpr1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of exports to price.  Elxpr1 and elxpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elxpr2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of exports to change in price.  Elxpr1 and elxpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: migratebalancesw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to balance between bilateral migration (1) and monadyc migration (0)

nodes.NAME: edqualpriallm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education quality, primary, multiplier.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: actreaon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Action-reaction switch.  A value of 1 (as in the base case) turns on an action-reaction dynamic in the determination of threat.  A value of 0 turns it off.

nodes.NAME: agconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Agriculture demand convergence time, represents the time required  for agricultural demand to converge to the function's predicted values, in years. Initial country data may deviate from cross-sectional predictions due to possible data errors or unique country factors. This parameter assumes that over time, such discrepancies will align with the predicted values. A high value like 10000 stops convergence; a low value like 10 speeds it up.

nodes.NAME: clpcm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on per capita calorie demand, by region and without units. A value of 1 indicates no change; higher values increase demand, and lower values decrease it. Avoid changing the initial year's value; instead, adjust the multiplier over time.

nodes.NAME: aginvm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on agriculture investment, by region and without units. A value of 1 indicates no change. Values greater than 1 increase investment proportionally, and values less than 1 decrease it. Avoid changing the initial year value; instead, adjust the multiplier over time.

nodes.NAME: agon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Agriculture switch turns on or off the linkages  between the agricultural submodel and all others, including economy. A value of 1 turns the linkages on; 0 turns them off. Useful for isolating submodels during analysis. Typically set to 1.

nodes.NAME: hivculf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Cultural region-specific spread rate of HIV, expressed in percentage terms. For example, a value of 0.3 means 0.3% growth in spread rate each year.  This parameter is set for broad cultural regions such as the Islamic world and the  values have generally been set so that historic growth patterns coincide with actual tendencies in the region.

nodes.NAME: co2prein
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that defines the pre-industrial level of atmospheric CO2 in parts per million. Normally, a user would not change this parameter over time. See also carprein - that sets the pre-industrial atmospheric carbon levels in billion tons.

nodes.NAME: hlmortmodsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for mortality modification. A value of 2 turns on the Modification for the Human Capital (Education) term and for the Technology (Time) term, in both cases using the WHO low-income-model clasification (WHO 2002 version).  A value of 1 turns on the Modification for the Technology (Time) term using the IFs low-income clasification ($3k/cap), default is 1-On in the base case (2004 WHO version). A value of 0 turns it off and leaves mortality unchanged .

nodes.NAME: edtergradgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, tertiary, graduation rate, annual additive growth. A parameter to make the countries meet education targets by an annual additive growth in the rate of graduation in tertiary level.

nodes.NAME: elndpow
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of nuclear damage with nuclear power.  Values (normally positive) near 0 would imply little elasticity and values near 1 would imply very considerable elasticity.  Changes in this parameter will only have an effect when the model generates a nuclear war.

nodes.NAME: elprst1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of prices to stock/inventory levels.  Elprst1 and elprst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: waterhhm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for the percentage of people living with different levels of access to drinking water. Values greater than 1 raises access relative to the base case value for the same year. Values lower than 1 reduce access.

nodes.NAME: sanithhcostlowershr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, Sanitation services, share of services using lower-cost service. Base case value is 50/50 when both lower and upper cost services are available

nodes.NAME: watsafenewsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, water and Sanitation 5 Category Switch, 1 will use 5 category for infrastructure spending and forward linkage

nodes.NAME: waterhhlifepiped
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, safe water connections, piped, lifetime in years

nodes.NAME: waterhhlifeboreholetubewell
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, safe water connections, borehole or tubewell, lifetime in years

nodes.NAME: waterhhlifedugwell
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, safe water connections, dugwell, lifetime in years

nodes.NAME: sanithhlifesst
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, sanitation, septic, sewerage, treatment facilities, lifetime in years

nodes.NAME: sanithhlifepitlatrinebasic
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, sanitation, basic pit latrine, lifetime in years

nodes.NAME: sanithhlifepitlatrinetrad
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, sanitation, rural traditional pit latrine, lifetime in years

nodes.NAME: sanithhbasictrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sanitation services, at least basic, target value to be reached by a certain number (sanithhbasictrgtyr) of years starting from the model base year. Default value is 100.

nodes.NAME: sanithhm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for the percentage of people living with different levels of access to sanitation services. Values greater than 1 raises access relative to the base case value for the same year. Values lower than 1 reduce access.

nodes.NAME: ageofmarriagetfrelas
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Responsiveness of TFR to changes in average age of marriage from expected value, i.e., base case forecast. A value of .01 will decrease TFR by .01 when age of marriage is one year more than the base case forecast.

nodes.NAME: foodinsecuritym
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Food Security Index. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: womeninleadershipm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on managerial roles filled by women. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: unpaidlaborm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on unpaid labor force. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: watsafefwdsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure, water and Sanitation 5 Category Switch, 1 will use 5 category for forward linkage, 0 will use 3 category for forward linkage. This does not affect spending.

nodes.NAME: waterbudgetprotec
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is for budget protection of water services spending. (1 = full protection, 0 is no protection) Values in between 0 and 1 indicates the share of demanded budget that will be set aside of the normalization process.

nodes.NAME: sanitbudgetprotec
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is for budget protection of sanitation services spending. Values greater than 1 raises the cost relative to the base case value for the same year. Values lower than 1 lowers the cost.

nodes.NAME: infrabudgetprotec
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is for budget protection by infrastructure type. (1 = full protection, 0 is no protection) Values in between 0 and 1 indicates the share of demanded budget that will be set aside from the budget allocated for infrastructure in the government finance model.

nodes.NAME: elprst2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of prices to change in stock/inventory levels.  Elprst1 and elprst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: govcorruptm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government corruption index.

nodes.NAME: tefinfadjm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the adjustment of productivity (TEF) because of the extent of informal economy. A value of 0 indicates no adjustment and a value of 1 indicates full adjustment.

nodes.NAME: gdpinformshrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the informal share of GDP.

nodes.NAME: hlincoefgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: GBD Regression's Income coefficient growth.

nodes.NAME: hlgbdconvDown
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence time coefficient for bringing initial adjustments/normalization factors towards 1, downward convergence only

nodes.NAME: envylchgadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Global additive shift factor for the annual change in agricultural yield by country/region.

nodes.NAME: hltechshift
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the technological shift factor to alter technological change, proportional to GDP per capita.

nodes.NAME: envco2fert
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Effect of CO2 fertilization on crop yields.

nodes.NAME: sanithldsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to hold the forecast of Sanitation at Base year levels

nodes.NAME: watsafhldsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to hold the forecast of Safe Water at Base year levels

nodes.NAME: ensolflhldsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to hold the forecast of Solid Fuel Use at Base year levels

nodes.NAME: envpm25hldsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to hold the forecast of residential PM2.5 air pollution levels. A value of 0 indicates off; 1 indicates on.

nodes.NAME: malnhldsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to hold the forecast of malnutrition among children.

nodes.NAME: sfmassrep
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for state failure mass repression. A value of 1 turns on totalitarian system-like repression that suppresses domestic conflict of any kind and value of 0 represents no such change (default case).

nodes.NAME: infrainvmaintpubshrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the public share in funding maintenance of infrastructure of a specific type.

nodes.NAME: infrainvnewpubshrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the public share in funding maintenance of infrastructure of a specific type.

nodes.NAME: hlmortm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on mortality.

nodes.NAME: hlmorbtomortgthport
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter controls the rate of growth of morbidity relative to mortality. For example, Cardio Vascular Disease has a value of 0.5, indicating that for each unit of decrease in CVD mortality there's only a decrease of 0.5 in CVD morbidity

nodes.NAME: labmarketsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to turn on the impact of changes in labor demand to computation of value added (normally supply affects it and changes more slowly)

nodes.NAME: elwageunemp1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: First parameter in PID controller that links unemployment level  to change in labor wage index.

nodes.NAME: elwageunemp2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Second parameter in PID controller that links change in unemployment level  to change in labor wage index.

nodes.NAME: ellabwage1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: First parameter in PID controller that links labor wage index  to change in labor demand

nodes.NAME: elfdilifexp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of foreign direct investment to gains in years of life expectancy.

nodes.NAME: protecm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on trade protection, by region allows user to adjust the price of imported goods, relative to the base case. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the prices of imported goods and lower values decrease them.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: ensolfuelsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of Standard Errors to be targeted by the forecast (between -2 and 2), 0 turns off the targetting.

nodes.NAME: ensolfuelseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of years to target a given number of Standard Errors by the forecast.

nodes.NAME: extmafuncelectran
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter decides the moving average factor for the growthrate required to move along the function.

nodes.NAME: extmafuncroad
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter decides the moving average factor for the growthrate required to move along the function.

nodes.NAME: extmafuncroadpaved
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter decides the moving average factor for the growthrate required to move along the function.

nodes.NAME: extmaposnconvtimeelectran
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter represents the time required to converge to the function from the current position.

nodes.NAME: extmaposnconvtimeroad
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter represents the time required to converge to the function from the current position.

nodes.NAME: mprconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the convergence time of Materialism/postmaterialism to expected valye based on the analytic function. Very often initial data values for countries will differ a little or much from values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

nodes.NAME: resorm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Ultimately recoverable resource multiplier, by energy type.  This parameter allows the user to increase or decrease ultimately recoverable resource values.  A value of 1 accepts the values of RESOR as specified.  A value of 1.5 would raise the resource levels for a specific energy form in a specific country/region by 50 percent.  This multiplier is unusual in that it is only important in the first year - it should not be changed over time because after ultimate resources are calculated the first year they can only run down (be used up).

nodes.NAME: slr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Livestock slaughter rate coefficient represents the proportion of herd slaughtered annually. For example, a rate of 0.7 means 70% of the herd is slaughtered each year.

nodes.NAME: wagnerc
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Wagner's law coeficient; annual growth in govt expenditures.  Wagner's Law (from the late 1800s) said that government expenditures would continue to increase as a portion of GDP.  Although this effect must ultimately saturate (the model limits it), it has continued into the 21st century.  You can set a value in terms of annual percentage increase (or decrease) in government/GDP. Thus, 1 = 1% annual increase in the ratio.

nodes.NAME: infrafinon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infrastructure Finance Model Switch.  A value of 1 (as in the base case) turns the infrastructure public financing code. 0 turns off the connection

nodes.NAME: carstotm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on total car sales by country/region.  A value of 1.0 leaves total sales unchanged.  An increase over time to 2.0 would approximately double total sales relative to the base case (sales by type will not always change proportionately, because of differing relationships with total sales).

nodes.NAME: truckstotm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on total truck sales by country/region.  A value of 1.0 leaves total sales unchanged.  An increase over time to 2.0 would approximately double total sales relative to the base case (sales by type will not always change proportionately, because of differing relationships with total sales).

nodes.NAME: ictbroadmobiltrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal access to mobile broadband

nodes.NAME: ictbroadtrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal access to fixed broadband

nodes.NAME: infraroadraitrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal access to roads.

nodes.NAME: carsconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence time for car sales in years. This value determines the number of years over which all countries/regions will converge to the chosen function (as determined by the switch, vehfuncsw) for the computation of car sales per year.  A value of 10000 would effectively turn off convergence, so that initial country-specific variations from the function would be maintained over time.  A value of 60 would lead to near convergence by the middle of the 21st century.  Very rapid convergence seems improbable in the face of fundamental country differences in infrastructure, land area, culture, etc.

nodes.NAME: edpriintngr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education Primary Net Intake Rate Anuual Growth Rate. A parameter to make the countries meet education targets by an annual percentage growth in net intake rate.

nodes.NAME: edprisurgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education Primary Survival Rate Annual Growth Rate. A parameter to make the countries meet education targets by an annual percentage growth in survival rate.

nodes.NAME: edseclowrtrangr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, lower secondary (general), transion rate from primary, annual additive growth. A parameter to make the countries meet education targets by an annual additive growth in the rate of transition from primary to general lower secondary.

nodes.NAME: edtergndreqint
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education tertiary, no of years by which gender parity index for intake rate raeches 1. The gender parity index is the ratio of the male rate to the female rate.

nodes.NAME: edtergndreqgrad
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education tertiary, no of years by which gender parity index for graduation rate reaches 1. The gender parity index is the ratio of the male rate to the female rate. Must set edgndreqsuron=1 for this to work.

nodes.NAME: edsecupprgndreqtran
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education upper sec, no of years by which gender parity index for transition rate raeches 1. The gender parity index is the ratio of the male rate to the female rate.

nodes.NAME: ldcropm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on crop land, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase crop land and lower values decrease it.

nodes.NAME: goveffectseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies that number of years to reach the standard error target for GOVEFFECT.

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingdecm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on exponential/logarithmic rate of decrease in smoking among adults aged above 30.

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingfloor
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Minimum smoking prevalence among adults aged over 30.

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingincm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on exponential rate of increase in smoking among adults aged above 30.

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingpeakyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Peak year of smoking prevalence among adults aged over 30. When peak year is set to "on" prevalence begins to fall after specified year.

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingstsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This switch turns on the 4 stages of smoking prevalence.

nodes.NAME: agstkadjsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Agricultural stock change switch eliminates the impact of supply and demand imbalances on agricultural food stocks.  A value of 1 turns on the switch for highly specialized scenarios.

nodes.NAME: agtrdadjsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Agricultural trade switch eliminates the impact of domestic and international food stocks changes on trade ratios. A value of 1 turns on the switch for highly specialized scenarios.

nodes.NAME: agmm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on agricultural imports, by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase investment and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: HLSTUNTCHL
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The percentage of children under 5 that is affected by childhood malnutrition

nodes.NAME: watpricetoylelas
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity that helps create a multiplier on yield by multiplying the ratio of change in water price relative to base water price and adding to 1.

nodes.NAME: wpindsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A switch that can be used to turn on or off the calculations of Character of Bilateral State Interaction Score.  A value of 0 turns it off and a value greater than 0 turns it on.  1 is used to save threat, 2 is used to save Liberal Index, 3 is used to save Realist Index and 4 is used to save the COI.

nodes.NAME: ictmobilsetar

nodes.NAME: infraelecaccsetar

nodes.NAME: infraelecaccseyrtar

nodes.NAME: ellabwage2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Second  parameter in PID controller that links change in labor wage index to change in labor demand

nodes.NAME: hdiedyrsmaxun
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the maximum education years for adults aged over 25, used for calculation of education component in HDI. Users will normally not change this parameter.

nodes.NAME: hdilifemaxun
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the maximum life expectancy, used for calculation of  HDI component. Users will normally not change this parameter.

nodes.NAME: hdiedslemaxun
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the maximum school life expectancy in education, used for calculation of education component in HDI. Users will normally not change this parameter.

nodes.NAME: edqualag15m
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education quality, adult 15+ score, multiplier.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: infraroadraitrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the value of percentage access considered as universal access to all weather roads within two kilometers for people in the rural areas.

nodes.NAME: edsecupprtrancap
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for setting the upper limit on transition or survival in upper secondary (1= cap transition)

nodes.NAME: desald
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Responsiveness of water price to change in prices.

nodes.NAME: druguseamphetaminem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the use of amphetamine drug.

nodes.NAME: drugusecocainem

nodes.NAME: druguseopiatesm

nodes.NAME: druguseprescriptopioidm

nodes.Parameter Explanation: Potentially arable land represents the maximum crop land value for each country based on the medium value from Eitelberg et al. 2015

nodes.NAME: drugglobalconvsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for global convergence in drug use.

nodes.NAME: svdthsadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive factor on societal violence deaths.

nodes.NAME: govindsecurconflict
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Government security index term for conflict.

nodes.NAME: govindsecurgovrisk
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Government security index term for for government risk.

nodes.NAME: govindsecurviolence
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Government security index term for for violence.

nodes.NAME: edqualsecspndimp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A multiplier that determines the impact of additional per student spending (as a percentage share of GDPPC) on education quality score. For example, a value of .5 would mean changing per student spending by 1 percentage point, e.g., from 10% of per capita income to 11% of the same, will add .5 to the quality score for the level of education..

nodes.NAME: edqualprispndimp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A multiplier that determines the impact of additional per student spending (as a percentage share of GDPPC) on education quality score. For example, a value of .5 would mean changing per student spending by 1 percentage point, e.g., from 10% of per capita income to 11% of the same, will add .5 to the quality score for the level of education..

nodes.NAME: svtohlsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to activate linkage between societal violence and health. A value of 1 indicates on; 0 indicates off.

nodes.NAME: edexperterm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on tertiary per student expenditure (as % of gdppc).

nodes.NAME: govindsecurm

nodes.NAME: edqualsecur
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of the impact of societal insecurity  on education quality score.

nodes.NAME: edenrsecur

nodes.NAME: edqualsecspndimpgov

nodes.NAME: edqualsecspndimpthreshold
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A parameter to turn off/tune the impact of nearing threshold on the spending impacts on secondary education quality.

nodes.NAME: edqualprispndimpgov
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A parameter to turn off/tune the impact of governance on the spending impacts on primary education quality.

nodes.NAME: edqualprispndimpthreshold
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A parameter to turn off/tune the impact of nearing threshold on the spending impacts on primary education quality.

nodes.NAME: idsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on investment, by sector and region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase investment and lower values decrease it. Investment across sectors are normalized. Thus changes in one sector will affect others. Patameter invm should be used to change total investment. Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: edqualsecspndimpthresholdval

nodes.NAME: edqualprispndimpthresholdval

nodes.NAME: edqualprimathm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education quality, primary, math score multiplier.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: edqualprireadm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education quality, primary, reading score multiplier.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: svvionormsw

nodes.NAME: labwageincfac

nodes.NAME: aidrecgovconp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Aid, share of aid received that is disbursed towards government consumption spending (the rest is used as transfer).

nodes.NAME: edterpushon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, parameter to slow down the impacts on tertiary enrollment from an education push at the lower levels of education

nodes.NAME: malnchpsamm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM).  A value of 1 represents no change, 1.25 represents a 25 percent increase and .75 represents a 25 percent decrease.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: samadmissionm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on percentage of SAM cases admitted for treatment. A value of 1 represents no change, 1.25 represents a 25 percent increase and .75 represents a 25 percent decrease.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: samavertedm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Mutliplier on the percentage of SAM cases successfully treated. A value of 1 represents no change, 1.25 represents a 25 percent increase and .75 represents a 25 percent decrease.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: malnchpsamtostunt
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of SAM on stunting. This parameter is used to increase or decrease the effect of severe acute malnutrition on stunting.

nodes.NAME: samadmissioncost
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the cost per SAM admission.

nodes.NAME: samrrsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to turn on/off the relative risk effect of SAM.

nodes.NAME: diploingoadvocacym
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the number of advocacy INGOs operating in, on or about a country.

nodes.NAME: diploingoprogramm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the number of programmatic INGOs operating in, on or about a country.

nodes.NAME: malnelimstartyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the starting year towards elimination of hunger. It works in combination with malnelimtargetyr.

nodes.NAME: malnelimtargetyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the target year towards elimination of hunger. It works in combination with malnelimstarttyr.

nodes.NAME: malelimprecisesw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for elimination of hunger; brings only the hungry population up to 1844 (no hunger) calorie level; adds to calorie needs.

nodes.NAME: malnchpsamadj
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Adjustment parameter for incidence of Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM).  A value of 1 represents Incidence is equal to prevalence. Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: samadmissionadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive factor for percentage of SAM cases admitted for treatment.

nodes.NAME: samadmissionsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for percentage of SAM cases admitted for treatment. A value of 0 shows regular forecast, 1 keeps zeroes constant and a value of 2 keep all constant.

nodes.NAME: hlstuntyrs
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the moving average of stunting years.

nodes.NAME: samavertedconvyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence time for averted SAM cases.

nodes.NAME: edbudgon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, parameter to turn budget impact off. Base case value is 1 (=budget impact on). Set it to 0 to bypass budget impacts entirely.

nodes.NAME: eprodr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy production growth rate, expressed in decimal form (e.g., 0.035 equals 3.5 percent annual growth, by region and fuel type. This parameter can override endogenous patterns of energy production growth and force a pattern of growth for a specific fuel or set of fuels.  Growth rates are, however, constrained in the model by the availability of investment and/or resources, and may not be met.  Only positive values are allowed.  Under most circumstances, the initial value for this variable should be equal to that of enprr for the specified region and fuel type, because enprr is the empirical initial growth rate.

nodes.NAME: eprohw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy profits, historic (inertial delay) in impact on investment.  Values near 1.0 imply very rapid adjustment and values near 0 imply little or no adjustment.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: etechadv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy technology advance rate (decrease in cost of energy production), expressed in decimal form (e.g. 0.01 equals 1 percent annual growth, by energy type).  Use, for example, to decrease the cost of renewable energy over time.  A value of 0.01 applied to renewable energy would force an annual decrease in the costs of producing solar energy of 1% each year, representing continued technological advance in such production (a value of -0.01 would represent a negative cost decrease, that is, a cost increase).

nodes.NAME: eleniprof2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy investment to change in profit level.  Eleniprof and eleniprof2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: migrater
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Net migration of a population in percent per year (negative values reflect emigration and positive values reflect immigration).  Because global emigration and immigration must balance, changes in this value for a single country/region may not change migration/population as substantially as the change introduced in migrater.

nodes.NAME: enrgdpgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Annual percentage change in energy demand as a result of technological change.  This parameter helps represent the historic phenomenon of considerable decrease over time in energy requirements per unit of economic output ("dematerialization").  It is an uncertain but very important parameter.  A value of -1 would represent an annual efficiency improvement of 1 percent.

nodes.NAME: elastrpr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of trade with prices, by economic sector. A value of 1 implies a 1% increase in exports when local prices are 1% below world prices, and a similar increase in imports when local prices are 1% above world prices. Values generally range from 0 to 2 and remain constant over time. This parameter interacts with parameters elmpr1, elmpr2, elxpr1, and elxpr2, all of which play a role in the equilibrium-seeking structure of the economic/trade model.  Unfortunately, the collective meaning of these trade parameters in conventional elasticity terms is not as clear as it should be, because they have been set to assure market-clearing behavior.

nodes.NAME: mfpconv2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence of Multifactor Productivity Growth in ICT represents the time (in years) for productivity to converge to that of the service sector.

nodes.NAME: numnwpgrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on growth rate of number of networked persons. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase investment and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: hdigdppcmax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: GDP per capita calculation for HDI calculation in thousands.  Users may change the parameter to represent changing global possibilities..

nodes.NAME: lvcf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Livestock to calorie conversion factor, compared to crops.

nodes.NAME: hlbednetsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on availability of bednet. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: sanitationm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for the percentage of People living with different levels of Access to Sanitation

nodes.NAME: wpsysgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, change in dispute probability with global economic growth. The value is in percent. Thus 0.1 would indicate that the probability of a dispute between two states would rise by 0.1% for each percentage point increase in global economic growth relative to the long-term average.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted from other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

nodes.NAME: democpolitysetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter sets the target standard errors to be forecasted for DEMOC. Values range between -2 to 2, with 0 indicating that the target standard errors are turned off. This parameter is used in combination with democpolityseyrtar.

nodes.NAME: democpolityseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter sets the number of years to a given standar error target of DEMOC.

nodes.NAME: govregqualsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the target standard errors for GOVREGQUAL forecast. Value range between -2 to 2, with 0 indicating that the target is turned off. Used in combination with govregqualseyrtar.

nodes.NAME: govregqualseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies that number of years to reach the standard error target for GOVREGQUAL.

nodes.NAME: gemsetar
