nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the target standard errors for GEM forecast. Value range between -2 to 2, with 0 indicating that the target is turned off. Used in combination with gemseytar.

nodes.NAME: govcorruptsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the target standard errors for GOVCORRUPT forecast. Value range between -2 to 2, with 0 indicating that the target is turned off. Used in combination with govcorruptseyrtar.

nodes.NAME: hlsmokingtcsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on tobacco control score. Used when the switch hlsmokingstsw is set to 1.

nodes.NAME: deathtrpvseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies that number of years to reach the standard error target for DEATHTRPV.

nodes.NAME: deathtrpvsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the target standard errors for DEATHTRPV forecast. Value range between -2 to 2, with 0 indicating that the target is turned off. Used in combination with deathtrpvseyrtar.

nodes.NAME: extmaposnconvtimeroadpaved
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter represents the time required to converge to the function from the current position.

nodes.NAME: extmaposnelectran
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter decides the moving average factor for the growthrate required to converge to the function from the current position.

nodes.NAME: extmaposnenelecshr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter decides the moving average factor for the growthrate required to converge to the function from the current position.

nodes.NAME: extmaposnroad
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter decides the moving average factor for the growthrate required to converge to the function from the current position.

nodes.NAME: extmaposnroadpaved
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter decides the moving average factor for the growthrate required to converge to the function from the current position.

nodes.NAME: ictbroadmobilsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of Standard Errors to be targeted by the forecast (between -2 and 2), 0 turns off the targetting.

nodes.NAME: ictbroadmobilseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of years to target a given number of Standard Errors by the forecast.

nodes.NAME: ictbroadsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of Standard Errors to be targeted by the forecast (between -2 and 2), 0 turns off the targetting.

nodes.NAME: ictbroadseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of years to target a given number of Standard Errors by the forecast.

nodes.NAME: watsafetrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal access to safe water (through improved or household connection)

nodes.NAME: edseclowrlen
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Duration of education, lower secondary is the number of grades (years) in lower secondary education, aggregation rule for group might result in non-integer values

nodes.NAME: edsecupprlen
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Duration of education, Upper secondary is the number of grades (years) in Upper secondary education, aggregation rule for group might result in non-integer values

nodes.NAME: sanitnoconsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of Standard Errors to be targeted by the forecast (between -2 and 2), 0 turns off the targetting.

nodes.NAME: sanitnoconseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of years to target a given number of Standard Errors by the forecast.

nodes.NAME: watsafenoconsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of Standard Errors to be targeted by the forecast (between -2 and 2), 0 turns off the targetting.

nodes.NAME: watsafenoconseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of years to target a given number of Standard Errors by the forecast.

nodes.NAME: watwastetreatsetar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of Standard Errors to be targeted by the forecast (between -2 and 2), 0 turns off the targetting.

nodes.NAME: watwastetreatseyrtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sets the number of years to target a given number of Standard Errors by the forecast.

nodes.NAME: mfpdemoc
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Democracy contribution to MFP.

nodes.NAME: infraelecaccurbancostm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter can be used to change the unit cost for a particular country or region relative to the base case.

nodes.NAME: landircostlower
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that sets a global lower bound value on per hectare cost of irrigation.

nodes.NAME: landircostupper
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that sets a global upper bound value on per hectare cost of irrigation.

nodes.NAME: sanitationimpcostm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter to change the unit cost relative to the base case.

nodes.NAME: watsafeimpcostm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter to change the unit cost relative to the base case.

nodes.NAME: watsafetrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the value of percentage with no access considered as universal access to safe water (for example, 0 percent)

nodes.NAME: sanitationtrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the  value of percentage with household connections considered as universal access to sanitation.

nodes.NAME: malnm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multplier on malnutrition among the population. A value of 1 represents no change, 1.25 represents a 25 percent increase and .75 represents a 25 percent decrease.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: edseclowrgndreqtran
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education lower sec, no of years by which gender parity index for transition rate raeches 1. The gender parity index is the ratio of the male rate to the female rate.

nodes.NAME: edseclowrtrancap
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for setting the upper limit on transition or survival in lower secondary (1= cap transition)

nodes.NAME: edprigoalexperon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education Per Primary Student expenditure (as a % of GDPPC) Goal Seek Switch. A parameter to turn goal seek on. Works with edprigoalexper

nodes.NAME: edprigoalexper
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education Per Primary Student expenditure (as a % of GDPPC) Goal. A parameter to make the countries meet per student expenditure goals, e.g. bes practices. You must set edprigoalexperon to 1 for this to work.

nodes.NAME: elagind
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of industrial (incl energy) use of crops with energy price.  0 turns it off.

nodes.NAME: ylmaxgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that roughly controls the the maximum increase in agricultural yields (.05 would be 5% annually).  It is phased downward at the hhighest values of current yields.

nodes.NAME: calmax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Maximum kilocalories needed per person per day. This biologically determined value should generally not change over time.

nodes.NAME: calmeatm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Maximum proportion of calories from meat, increasing with income up to this cap. The value, between 0 and 1, is typically set only in the first year.

nodes.NAME: caputtar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Capacity utilization target level, expressed as a ratio. For example, a target level of 0.8 signifies that the capacity utilization should reach 80% of full use. Typically, this value would remain unchanged across all years.

nodes.NAME: carinit
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Initial level of carbon dioxide in atmosphere in the base year, expressed in billion tons. The value in the model should be relatively accurate.

nodes.NAME: edprigndreqsur
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education primary, no of years (from firstyear) by which gender parity in primary survival rate is reached. The gender parity index is the ratio of the male rate to the female rate. Must set edgndreqsuron=1 for this to work.

nodes.NAME: carprein
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that defines the pre-industrial atmospheric carbon levels, expressed in billion tons. Normally, a user will not change this parameter over time.

nodes.NAME: xfdifinm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on annual FDI invesment inflows. A value of 1 implies no change.

nodes.NAME: cdmf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Civilian damage factor.  This reactivity parameter links the severity of conventional war and the power of the opposing alliance to civilian damage (both population killed and economic capital destroyed).  A value of 0 will uncouple conventional war from damage and a value of 1 will make damage proportional to the war severity and opposing power.  There is no comparable parameter for the impact of nuclear war on civilians because the model always assumes civilian damage; in fact, it extends some such damage beyond the regions involved in nuclear war to third party countries (from fall-out and other collateral damage).

nodes.NAME: clnf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Calorie need factor or multiplier on calorie needs, by region. Usually set at 1. It adjusts regional calorie requirements to address food shortages impacting infant mortality. A value of 0 turns off the feedback between food shortages and infant mortality for a region.

nodes.NAME: clsexp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Exponent parameter that links calorie shortage to starvation. Higher values lower starvation and lower values increase starvation.

nodes.NAME: xwbsectar
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World Bank Sector Target, Shares in Percent.

nodes.NAME: GINIDOM
nodes.Parameter Explanation: No longer used as a parameter (is computed as a variable).  See, instead, incshrm.

nodes.NAME: hdilifemaxf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Life expectancy minimum for HDI calculation, in years.  Users may change the parameter to represent growing life expectancy.

nodes.NAME: hivpeakyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the peak year of HIV infection. It controls the year in which the rate of infection in a population reaches its peak, before the epidemic begins to wane.

nodes.NAME: GOVRISK
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The Risk Index is a weigthed average of the contribution to risk of a set of aproximately 20 variables. Each variable can contribute from 0 to 1 depending on where its value sits in the Minimum to Maximum range.

nodes.NAME: ictbroadfromtelem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for proportion of fixed telephone divestment that is used for fixed broadband

nodes.NAME: ensolfueltrgtval
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the target value of percentage of people using solid fuel.

nodes.NAME: enml
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy import limit, expressed in billion barrels of oil equivalent functions both as a switch and a numerical value, with 0 indicating no limit and positive values setting a specific limit. Positive values (above .001) limit imports to the value specified.  For instance, a specification for a country of 0 for the first five years, 2 for the next three, and 0 thereafter,  introduces a constrain on imports of two billion barrels per year during the sixth, seventh, and eighth years.  Restrictions of this kind are more often posed by exporters (see enxl) than importers.

nodes.NAME: democimpoth
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the democracy impetus from non-specific forces such as the spread of a systemic value around democracy. The scale ranges from 1-10 (10=most) and is based on the Polity scale.  Normally interventions with the parameter would be variable over time (e.g., increasing gradually).

nodes.NAME: democimpusn
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The neutral or normal level of democracy impetus coming from US or other (e.g., EU) leadership.  The scale ranges from 1-10 (10=most) and is based on the Polity democracy scale.   Interventions with the parameter would be very uncommon and would normally change its value for all points in time.

nodes.NAME: eldemocimp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of democracy levels with systemic leadership.  That is, the responsiveness of democracy in a country to the impetus towards democracy provided by countries/regions such as the EU or the U.S.

nodes.NAME: malemigr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Male migration as a portion of total migration.  This parameter is expressed as a ratio value, so that .47 would mean 47%.

nodes.NAME: livhdpro
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Represents the productivity gains in livestock herds due to grain feeding, functioning as a multiplier-index. Normally, users should adjust this value gradually, starting with the initial value.

nodes.NAME: aiddon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Aid (foreign) donations as % of GDP.  A coefficient of foreign assistance, by country/region.  It is in percentage form and is the percentage of GDP given in foreign aid (e.g., -0.2 equals 0.2 percent of GDP).

nodes.NAME: squeez
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A switch that squeezes economic production when there are energy shortages (IFs does not force equilibration between energy supply and demand in any given time period, but seeks it over time; thus in the case of severe supply constraints, such as export limits by OPEC, actual shortages can appear).  A value of 0 turns off the linkage and the normal value of 1 activates it.  Other positive values also turn on the switch.  A value of 2 would make the impact of a shortage twice as great as normal and a value of 0.5 would cut it in half.

nodes.NAME: carabr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Rate of carbon absorption - this parameter defines the amoung of atmospheric carbon (expressed in billion tons) that oceans or other sinks (except forests) absorb each year. Although this value should ultimately be a function of the carbon in the atmosphere and the carbon in the sinks of the ocean, land, and biological systems (and hence a computed variable), it is common in atmospheric models to specify it as a single, constant parameter.

nodes.NAME: carbtax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that sets the carbon tax, expressed in dollars/ton of carbon generated and affects (increases) energy prices and (decreases) demand. Values will normally be above 50 and as an example, a value of 100 ($100/ton) will add about $0.20 to the price of a gallon of gas.

nodes.NAME: carforst
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Carbon generated by deforestation - this parameter specifies the amount of atmospheric carbon (expressed in billion tons) that will be added by deforestation (expressed in billion hectares of land). Normally you would not change this parameter over time, because it should be a fairly fixed parameter.

nodes.NAME: carfuel1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Carbon generated by burning oil, expressed in billion tons per billion barrels of oil equivalent.  Although this is an empirical value, it is possible that some advance technologies might sequester rather than release carbon into the atmosphere.

nodes.NAME: carfuel2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Carbon generated by burning natural gas expressed in billion tons per billion barrels of oil equivalent .  Although this is an empirical value, it is possible that some advance technologies might sequester rather than release carbon into the atmosphere.

nodes.NAME: carfuel3
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Carbon generated by burning coal expressed in billion tons per billion barrels of oil equivalent.  Although this is an empirical value, it is possible that some advance technologies might sequester rather than release carbon into the atmosphere.

nodes.NAME: xhw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Export propensity, inertial delay in change.  This parameter computes a moving average of export propensity.  A value of 0.7 would weight the historical or moving average by 0.7 and the newly computed value by 0.3 (1-0.7).

nodes.NAME: wpally
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, reduction of dispute threat with alliance in dyad.  The value is in percent probability of a dispute.  That is, -0.1 would indicate that being in an alliance would reduce the probability of a dispute between two states by 0.1%, all else being equal.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted from other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

nodes.NAME: xshift
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Export shift.  An additive parameter that allows increase (positive values) or decrease (negative values) of exports of materials, manufactured goods, and services, by region.  Changes will be offset automatically by changes in private and governmental consumption.  This variable can be used to implement export-led growth strategies.  The model bases each year's exports on the proportion of its product exported the previous year, so a value of 0.05 would add 5 percent to exports for that and subsequent years.  Because the impact is cumulative, values should seldom exceed 0.1.  The initial values of trade represent data, so xshift should be changed from zero only after the initial year.

nodes.NAME: hdiedsleminun
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the minimum school life expectancy in education, used for calculation of education component in HDI. Users will normally not change this parameter.

nodes.NAME: ylexp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Agricultural yields' exponent controlling saturation speed represents a slowdown in the rate of yield increases as they approach the maximum (ylmax), ensuring a gradual, asymptotic approach to the yield ceiling.

nodes.NAME: indirecttaxrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government taxes imposed on both households and firms for social security and welfare, expressed without units and by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase taxes and lower values decrease them.

nodes.NAME: ehw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy historical weight factor for impact of prices on demand.  This parameter controls the speed at which changes in energy prices effect demand.  Values near 1.0 imply very rapid adjustment and values near 0 imply little or no adjustment.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: envylchgm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for the annual change in agricultural yield by country/region.

nodes.NAME: hltechbase
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the technological factor when not using the low income model, instead only for high income countries.

nodes.NAME: hlobsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the effect on cardiovascular diseases when obesity changes from the expected values.

nodes.NAME: hlsmimpsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This switch is used to turn off the estimation of Smoking Impact, thus keeping the values constant after 2030. The GBD original forecast goes only until 2030.

nodes.NAME: hlvehsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch used to turn off the estimation of Smoking Impact, thus keeping the values constant after 2030. The GBD original forecast goes only until 2030.

nodes.NAME: edexptconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Tertiary per student expenditure as % of gdppc convergence time to function in years.  In the base case a shift from the function will be maintained because of the high convergence time.Scenarios with low convergence time make the per student cost rich those of high income countries as countries get richer. This increase in per student cost can come from lower pupil-teacher ratio, higher teacher salary and higher non-teacher salary portion of the cost.

nodes.NAME: elhlmortspn
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of mortality by type (Health Module Mortality) to health care expenditures.

nodes.NAME: ylhw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Exponent controlling saturation speed of agricultural yields.  This parameter computes a moving average of export propensity.  A value of 0.2 would weight the new value by 0.2 and the historical or moving average by 1-0.2 or 0.8.  This parameter helps maintain behavioral stability in the face of yields that may begin to reach their maximum (see ylmax and ylexp).

nodes.NAME: ylm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on agricultureal yields, by region. It is used to represent potential yield changes due to technological or environmental factors. The value is typically adjusted over time rather than in the initial year. For example, a value of 1 represents no change, 1.25 represents a 25 percent increase and .75 represents a 25 percent decrease.

nodes.NAME: TGRYL
nodes.Parameter Explanation: No longer used as a parameter, rather computed only.  See ylm and mfpadd.  The values are in decimal terms, so that a value of 0.001 would convey a rate of 1%.

nodes.NAME: mfpleadr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multifactor productivity growth rate of system leader.  This parameter is a powerful mechanism by which the user can increase or decrease the growth rate of productivity of the systemic leader (historically the U.S.).  Such changes pass through to assumptions of the rate of productivity growth in all other countries of the system.  A value of 0.01 introduces a rate of productivity growth of 1.0% annually in the systemic leader.

nodes.NAME: tmortr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Time-related reduction in mortality, in portion per year (i.e., .01 represents 1 percent).  Although time-related, it is obviously meant to represent the affect of technological advance on life expectancy.  This parameter is global, and you will often prefer to use mortm to introduce scenarios around mortality and life expectancy, because that parameter is country/region specific.

nodes.NAME: wpgreat2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, increment of dispute probability in dyad with two great powers.  The value is in percent probability of a dispute and is applied when at both members of the dyad are great powers (see wpgreatthesh and wpgreatlev for definitions of great power).  That is, 2.0 would indicate that the existence of two great powers would increase the probability of a dispute between two states by 2.0%, all else being equal.   Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted from other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).  This addition would be on top of the increment already added for the presence of one great power in a dyad (see wpgreat1).

nodes.NAME: rdinr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Rate of discovery of energy, basic annual increment.  This parameter determines the basic rate of additions to initial annual rates of fossil fuel discoveries.  That rate may not persist, however, because as resource bases near exhaustion, they gradually constrain discovery rates.

nodes.NAME: hlhivartm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the availability of HIV Anti-Retroviral Therapy.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: hlmalariaincm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on malaria incidence.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: hlmalariaprevm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on malaria prevalence.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: hlmalariamortm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on malaria mortality.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: hlhivincm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on HIV incidence. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: hlhivprevm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on HIV prevalence.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: hlhivmortm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on HIV mortality. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: wtempadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that sets the additive factor to the calculated global temperature.

nodes.NAME: co2perm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on atmospheric percentage of CO2.

nodes.NAME: hlcondomusem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the use of condoms among 15-24 year olds in high risk-sex cases. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: cconstsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Consumption constant switch, with 1 indicating on and 0 indicating off.

nodes.NAME: rdm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy reserve discovery multiplier, unit-less.  This parameter normally has a value of 1.  A value of 1.5 would increase annual fossil fuel discoveries by 50 percent (within the limit of ultimate resources, but without additional investment in energy discovery), while a value of 0.5 would decrease it by 50 percent.

nodes.NAME: reac
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Reactivity (Actor, Target).  This parameter determines the magnitude of the threat felt by a target in response to changing power balances with respect to an actor.  A value of 1.5 means that the perceived threat shifts 50 percent faster than the power balance, while a value of .5 means that threat rises only 50 percent as fast.  The user should be aware, however, that in the calculation of how threat affects defense spending, reactivities to ALL actors will shape a country's/region's expenditures, thus often diffusing sensitivity to changes in power of only a single external actor.  By setting reac for all actors towards a target to 0.0, then focusing the attention of a target on a single actor (e.g. reac(Russia, China) = 1.0), you can eliminate that diffusion of attention.

nodes.NAME: gdprext
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Computed in the preprocessor to set economic growth rates exogenously in early model years; it should be set to 0 when using gdpadjsw to determine growth.

nodes.NAME: nmilf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Nuclear military expenditure factor.  A coefficient determining what portion of a country's or region's military expenditure is devoted to nuclear weapons, including delivery systems.  For instance, 0.1 would result in 10 percent.  This can be changed over time and could be used to convert a traditionally nuclear-free region into a nuclear power.  Normal values will range from 0 to 0.2.

nodes.NAME: contrusm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Contraception use multiplier.  A multiplier on contraception use, by region.  It normally has a value of 1.  Higher values increase contraception use and lower values decrease it.

nodes.NAME: cpowdf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Conventional power damage factor.  This reactivity parameter links the severity of conventional war and the power of the opposing alliance to the losses of conventional power (personnel and equipment).  A value of 0 will uncouple conventional war from damage and a value of 1 will make damage proportional to the war severity and power of the opponents.

nodes.NAME: cwarbase
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Conventional warfare base probability - the model adds or substracts from this value incremental probabilities of war that depend on many factors (power balances, democracy levels, etc.).  Specify values between 0 and 1 for the base annual probability of war between any actor and target.  Normally the values should be quite near 0 and in the base case all values are set to zero.

nodes.NAME: cwarf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Conventional war factor.  If WarOn = 1, by setting the value of this parameter equal to 100 or more you can force the model to generate a wide-spread war. Use of this parameter is only recommended for testing the functioning of war in the model; it has no policy interpretation.

nodes.NAME: cwarsv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Conventional war severity factor.  This coefficient determines what portion of the conventional armament potential will be used when a war erupts.  Values should range from 0 (none) to 1 (all).

nodes.NAME: dkl
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Depreciation coefficient for agricultural land investment.  This scalar (not specific to country/region) indicates the portion (e.g., 0.01 is 1%) of the investment in agricultural land (e.g. terracing or irrigation) that depreciates in a given year.  Raising it would lead to greater requirements of agricultural investment in land to maintain that land in production.

nodes.NAME: enprixi
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy base equilibium price in dollars per barrel of oil equivalent, by region.  Energy price (ENPRI) is normally computed relative to a price given in the initial or base year.  If that price is consdered far from long-term equilibirum, this parameter can overide it endogenously.  If you set enprixi to positive, nonzero values, you can override the initial oil price with your own price level.

nodes.NAME: drcpow
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Annual depreciation rate of conventional power (coefficient).  It is in proportional terms so that 0.1 represents 10% depreciation annually.  High values could simulate arms control agreements that resulted in destruction of weapons.

nodes.NAME: drnpow
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Annual depreciation rate of nuclear power (coefficient).  It is in proportional terms so that 0.1 represents 10% depreciation annually.  High values could simulate arms control agreements that resulted in destruction of weapons.

nodes.NAME: dstl
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Desired level of stock or inventory within the economy, represented as a percentage. A value of 0.1, for instance, indicates a target stock level of 10% relative to the base case that often includes annual production and may also encompass demand, exports, or imports.

nodes.NAME: dstlen
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Desired energy stock level as portion of stock base.  It is in proportional terms so that 0.2 represents a 20% target stock level (of a base that usually includes annual production and may include demand, exports, or imports).  There is little reason for most users to want to change this parameter.

nodes.NAME: elinst1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of sectoral investment to stock level.  Elinst1 and elinst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elinst2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of sectoral investment to changes in stock level.  Elinst1 and elinst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: ellvhpr1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of livestock herd size to stock level.  Ellvhpr1 and ellvhpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: ellvhpr2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of livestock herd size to changes in stock level.  Ellvhpr1 and ellvhpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elmpr1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of imports to price.  Elmpr1 and elmpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elmpr2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of imports to changes in price.  Elmpr1 and elmpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elasit
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of total domestic demand to stocks/inventories. Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elasmd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of meat demand to prices.  Values (normally negative) near 0 imply little responsiveness of demand to prices and larger absolute values (near -1) imply considerable responsiveness.  This value normally will not change much over time.  Significant changes in the value from specification in the base case could lead to difficulties or instability in market clearing (balancing of supply and demand).

nodes.NAME: elass
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy supply with price change, by region and energy type.  There is tremendous uncertainty about these numbers.  Higher numbers will increase the responsiveness of energy supply to increased prices and lower numbers will decrease that responsiveness.  The elasticities actually work on energy investment and therefore only indirectly (and with a time delay) on energy supply.

nodes.NAME: elaszs
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of capacity utilization to stock/inventory level.  This is an adjustment parameters (not a true elasticity). Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior. This parameter is global in nature, and not currently active.

nodes.NAME: elenpr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy investment to inventory level.  Elenpr and elenpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elenpr2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy investment to change in inventory level.  Elenpr and elenpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elerca1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of exchange rate to capital account/GDP ratio.  Elerca1 and elerca2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elerca2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of exchange rate to change in capital account/GDP ratio.  Elerca1 and elerca2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: vehicflpcm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on vehicles per capita by country/region.  A value of 1.0 leaves vehicles per capita unchanged.  An increase over time to 2.0 would double vehicles per capita relative to the base case.

nodes.NAME: deathtrpvm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on deaths from traffic accidents per vehicle. A value of 1 leaves values unchanged, while a value of 2 would double death per vehicle relatibe to the base case.

nodes.NAME: hlmorttranssw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for mortality transition. When  Low Income countries make the transition from low-income to high income mortality, i.e. they start moving towards the high income regression for mortality.

nodes.NAME: HLSTUNT
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The percentage of the total population that is affected by childhood malnutrition

nodes.NAME: mfpstunt
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of multifactor productivity to stunting.

nodes.NAME: mfphlyld
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of multifactor productivity to years of life lost to disability.

nodes.NAME: ENVTPCHG
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The average annual temperature change from 1990 by country/region

nodes.NAME: watsafem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier for the percentage of People living with different levels of Access to Safe Water

nodes.NAME: tmortr2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Time-related reduction in mortality, in portion per year (i.e., .01 represents 1 percent). See and compare with tmortr; this represents catch-up in fertility reduction by poor countries using tech transfer.  Although time-related, it is obviously meant to represent the affect of technological advance on life expectancy.  This parameter is global, and you will often prefer to use mortm to introduce scenarios around mortality and life expectancy, because that parameter is country/region specific.

nodes.NAME: edprilen
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Duration of education, primary is the number of grades (years) in primary education, aggregation rule for group might result in non-integer values

nodes.NAME: edpristart
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Entrance age in primary education, aggregation rule for group might result in non-integer values

nodes.NAME: hlsolfuelsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the effect on respiratory diseases (and infections) when solid fuel use changes from the expected values.

nodes.NAME: hlpm2pt5sw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the effect on respiratory diseases and infections when residential PM2.5 level changes from the expected values.

nodes.NAME: ENVPRCHG
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The average annual precipitation change from 1990 by country/region

nodes.NAME: govconm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government consumption. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: swingstsdem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Swing state democracy effects from global, swing state, and regional democracy levels.  These parameters have been estimated and you will seldom change them. Values of 0 turn off the respective effects.

nodes.NAME: swseffmax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Swing State effects maximum annual magnitude (Polity points).  Because the Polity democracy scale runs from 1-10 (10=most democratic), you would normally not set a value for this parameter of more than 2-4 points, and most often it would be considerably lower.

nodes.NAME: democimpus
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Democracy impetus coming from US or other (e.g., EU) leadership.  Values are on a 1-10 (10=most) scale, related to the Polity democracy scale.  Normally interventions with the parameter would be variable over time (e.g., increasing gradually).

nodes.NAME: elfdpr1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of yield to stocks/inventories.  Elfdpr1 and elfdpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elfdpr2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of yield to changes in stocks/inventories.  Elfdpr1 and elfdpr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: swseffects
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Action-reaction switch.  A value of 1 (as in the base case) turns on an action-reaction dynamic in the determination of threat.  A value of 0 turns it off.

nodes.NAME: GINI
nodes.Parameter Explanation: No longer used as a parameter (is computed as a variable).  See, instead, incshrm.

nodes.NAME: freedomm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Freedom House's measure of freedom (FREEDOM), which combines civil and political scale ranging from 2 (most free) to 14 (least free). A value of 1 in the multiplier implies no change, while higher values increase the value of FREEDOM (making a country/region less free).

nodes.NAME: birthmshr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Births, male share.  Slightly more than 50% of births are males and more males die at most ages than do females.  This is an empirical value and you would normally not want to change it.

nodes.NAME: elasxinc
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of exports to production and income level.  Values (normally positive) near 0  imply little change of exports with income and values near 1 imply that exports increase or decrease proportionally with income.  Normally, values should not be set far from 1.  These are used on  Materials, Manufactrues, ICT and Services sectors.

nodes.NAME: elasminc
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of imports to income level.  Values (normally positive) near 0 imply little change of imports with income and values near 1 imply that imports increase or decrease proportionally with income. Typically, values are not set far from 1. These are used on Sectors Materials, Manufactrues, ICT and Services.

nodes.NAME: democm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the level of democracy, expressed without units and by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, users should not generally  change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: wvsagesw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for World Value Survets aging.  The parameter controls the dynamics associated with the value orientation of cohorts in the model.  The standard value for it is 2, which results in the "aging" of value orientations.  That is, value orientation is calculated from GDP per capita only for the youngest cohort; all others carry their orientation forward in time.  Any other value for wvsagesw (the WVS aging switch) will result in use of the cohort-specific functions with GDP per capita.

nodes.NAME: carsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on car sales by country/region and car type.  A value of 1.0 leaves car sales unchanged.  An increase over time to 2.0 would approximately double car sales of the specified type relative to the base case (total car sales will be normalized and therefore unchanged relative to the base case).

nodes.NAME: trucksm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on truck sales by country/region and truck type.  A value of 1.0 leaves truck sales unchanged.  An increase over time to 2.0 would approximately double truck sales of the specified type relative to the base case (total sales will be normalized and therefore unchanged relative to the base case).

nodes.NAME: cultshmp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Cultural shift on the materialism/post-materialism index.  It is an additive factor that represents the average "shift" in the index for materialism/post-materialism for a given cultural region (relative to what would be expected based of level of GDP per capita), as identified in the World Value Survey project.  The initial value is determined from data, but the user could change the value over time to represent cultural convergence or divergence.

nodes.NAME: cultshse
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Cultural shift on the survival/self-expression index.  It is an additive factor that represents the average "shift" in the index for survival/self-expression for a given cultural region (relative to what would be expected based of level of GDP per capita), as identified in the World Value Survey project.  The initial value is determined from data, but the user could change the value over time to represent cultural convergence or divergence.

nodes.NAME: contiguity
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The physical distance between two countries/reigons.  The scale is:  1=land contiguity; 2=0=12 miles; 3=12-24 miles; 4=24-150 miles; 5=150-400 miles; 6=more than 400 miles.  Normally you would not change this value over time.

nodes.NAME: govfinconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the convergence time of government financial balances to its global function. Very often initial data values for countries will differ a little or much from values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

nodes.NAME: xfdistockm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Foreign Direct Investment Stocks of Investments from Abroad.

nodes.NAME: xportfoliom
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on International Portfolio Investment, Inward Stocks.

nodes.NAME: ximfcrfinm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Credits from IMF, inflows.

nodes.NAME: xfdistoutm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Foreign Direct Investment (Outflows).

nodes.NAME: xportstoutm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Portfolio Investment, outward stocks.

nodes.NAME: ximfcreqr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: IMF Credit to Equity Ratio.

nodes.NAME: ximfcrrepr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: IMF credit repayment rate/time (Years).

nodes.NAME: ximfcrintr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on Credits from IMF, outflows (Repayments).

nodes.NAME: govexpm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government expenditure by destination.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: govrevm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government revenues by destination. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: elgrevdebt1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of government revenues to government debt levels.  Elprst1 and elprst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: wpgreatthresh
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, systemic power share for threshhold great power status.  The value is in percent of systemic power.  Thus 2.0 would indicate that a state was just beginning to be a great power when its share of total global power reached 2.0%. See also the level to be a full great power, wpgreatlev.

nodes.NAME: wpgreat1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, increment of dispute probability in dyad with one great power.  The value is in percent probability of a dispute and is applied when at least one member of the dyad is a great power (see wpgreatthesh and wpgreatlev for definitions of great power).  That is, 0.7 would indicate that the existence of one great power would increase the probability of a dispute between two states by 0.7%, all else being equal.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted from other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

nodes.NAME: prodtf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Production of energy, minimum reserve ratio.  This value specifies the minimum number of years of reserves, at current rates of production, that can exist for any fossil energy fuel.  Thus a value of 10 would mean that when reserves dropped below 10 years of production, production would be cut to restore the minimum ratio.

nodes.NAME: lks
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Lifetime of capital by sector, expressed in years.  You will normally only change this value slowly over time, maintaining the initial value.

nodes.NAME: tfrmin
nodes.Parameter Explanation: TFR (total fertility rate) stabilization level with high income.  This is a very important parameter, because fertility rates in many developed countries have falled well below the 2.1 replacement level.  The level at which they stabilize for countries at the highest levels of income, and when they stabilize (you might change this over time), will greatly effect ultimate global population maximums and possible decline rates.

nodes.NAME: tfrconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: TFR (total fertility rate) convergence time to expected value.  Very often initial data values for countries will differ a little or much from values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

nodes.NAME: hivpeakr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the peak rate of HIV infection. It controls the highest rate of infection in a population before the epidemic begins to wane.

nodes.NAME: hivpeakdef
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the default year of HIV epidemic peak.

nodes.NAME: goveffectm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government effectiveness index.

nodes.NAME: ssweltaxrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government taxes imposed on both households and firms for social security and welfare, expressed without units and by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase taxes and lower values decrease them.

nodes.NAME: hwf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Historical (inertial delay) weight in change of expected economic growth.  Values near 1.0 imply very rapid adjustment and values near 0 imply little or no adjustment.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: repayrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on loan repayment allows user to increase or decrease the target debt level.  A value of 0 means that all debt should be repayed (equilibrium dynamics will work around 0); values above 1 increase tolerance for debt.

nodes.NAME: resor
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Resources of fossil fuels, ultimate, billion barrels of oil equivalent.  This value only sets an initial condition; thereafter resources are computed taking into account depletion from production.

nodes.NAME: govhhtrnpenm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government to household transfers (pensions). A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier

nodes.NAME: govhhtrnwelm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government to household transfers for social welfare. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier

nodes.NAME: mfpbasinc
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Annual increment of growth in Multifactor Productivity Growth.

nodes.NAME: mfpinfict
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is currently inactive.

nodes.NAME: edexppconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Primary per student expenditure as % of gdppc convergence time to function in years.  In the base case a shift from the function will be maintained because of the high convergence time.Scenarios with low convergence time make the per student cost rich those of high income countries as countries get richer. This increase in per student cost can come from lower pupil-teacher ratio, higher teacher salary and higher non-teacher salary portion of the cost.

nodes.NAME: edsecupprtrangr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, upper secondary (general), transion rate from lower secondary, annual additive growth. A parameter to make the countries meet education targets by an annual additive growth in the rate of transition from general lower secondary to general upper secondary.

nodes.NAME: hlmodelsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter activates linkages between health and population. Turning it on (=1) would copy Health module results for LifeExpectancy to Population module, when off leaves them in LIFEXPTMP.

nodes.NAME: edterintgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Education, tertiary, intake rate, annual additive growth. A parameter to make the countries meet education targets by an annual additive growth in the rate of intake in tertiary level.

nodes.NAME: hltechssa
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the technological factor for Sub-Saharan Africa.

nodes.NAME: hltechlinc
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the technological factor for other low income countries.

nodes.NAME: watres
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Renewable water resources, expressed in cubic kilometers. This parameter is now purely informational, because IFs does not have a dynamic water model that uses it to constrain water use.

nodes.NAME: WATUSEPC
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Water use per capita.  Regional or country-specific water use per capita in million cubic meters per year.  It is only meaningful to change this value for the first year of model computation, because thereafter it rises or falls with crop production (implicitly with irrigation).  It is of interest to compare total computed water use (WATUSE) with water resources (watres).

nodes.NAME: ethnic1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the percentage of a country's/region's population identifying with the largest ethnic group in the population.  At this point the parameter is not linked to variables in the model, but it could at some point affect political stability.

nodes.NAME: ethnic2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the percentage of a country's/region's population identifying with the second largest ethnic group in the population.  At this point the parameter is not linked to variables in the model, but it could at some point affect political stability.

nodes.NAME: elenpst
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy production to world inventory level.  Elenpst and elenpst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elenpst2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy production to change in world inventory level.  Elenpst and elenpst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: eleniprof
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of energy investment to profit level.  Eleniprof and eleniprof2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: wpwghtpow
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, contribution of various components to power index.  This is a vector across all the allowable contributing variables in the calculation of state power.  Values of "1" turn on the contribution of a variable and values of "0" turn off the contribution.

nodes.NAME: hhtaxrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government taxes imposed on households by skill level, expressed without units and by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase taxes and lower values decrease them.

nodes.NAME: firmtaxrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government taxes imposed on firms, expressed without units and by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase taxes and lower values decrease them.

nodes.NAME: infmormax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Infant mortality maximum for PQLI calculation.  This value indicates an empirically-based value of minimum infant mortality levels (maximum in terms of quality of the value).  Users will normally not change the parameter.

nodes.NAME: invm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on all types of investment, by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase investment and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: xfdifoutm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on annual FDI invesment outflows. A value of 1 implies no change.

nodes.NAME: cexovals
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Consumption exogenous values is used to set consumption values exogenously, with a value of -100 to turn the setting off.

nodes.NAME: clpcexovals
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Exogenous values for Calories per Capita; set to -100 to turn off.

nodes.NAME: sanitationexovals
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sanitation Exogenous Values (-100 is off)

nodes.NAME: tfrexovals
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Total Fertility Rate Exogenous Values (-100 is off)

nodes.NAME: watsafeexovals
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Water Safety Exogenous Values (-100 is off)

nodes.NAME: hlmorthivmalsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for HIV and Malaria mortality. Turning it on (=1) would copy new forecast for HIV and Malaria on top of default Health module calculations, when off leaves them in HLHIVMORT and HLMALARIAMORT.

nodes.NAME: matmortratiom
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on maternal mortality rates.

nodes.NAME: wpcommun
nodes.Parameter Explanation: War probability elasticity with global community.  This parameter and the underlying level of global community (GLOCOM) are not now being used in the calculation of threat.

nodes.NAME: eumembsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: EU membership switch for caculations of power (0=none; 1= member).  The members of the European Union are, of course, known.  But as candidate members become full members, it would be appropriate to change the values of this parameter.

nodes.NAME: wpdemdist
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, response of dispute threat to political distance.  The value is in percent probability of a dispute and is applied to the absolute value of the distance in democracy level between the states in a dyad.  That is, 0.01 would indicate that every point of additional distance on the underlying Polity scale would increase the probability of a dispute between two states by 0.01%, all else being equal.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted from other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

nodes.NAME: wptrade
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, change in dispute threat with systemic trade.  The value is in percent. Thus -0.01% would indicate that the probability of a dispute between two states would fall by 0.01% for every percentage increase in world trade as a percent of global GDP.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted from other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

nodes.NAME: wpconmin
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, minimum power concentration affecting dispute probability.  This parameter bounds the power concentration range within which change affects dispute probability.

nodes.NAME: wpconmax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, maximum power concentration affecting dispute probability.  This parameter bounds the power concentration range within which change affects dispute probability.

nodes.NAME: elglinpr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of livestock grazing intensity to prices.  Values (normally positive) near 0 would imply little change of grazing with livestock prices and values near 1 would imply that grazing increases or decreases proportionally with prices.

nodes.NAME: eliasp1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of agricultural investment in land to economic return.  Eliasp1 and eliasp2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: eliasp2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of agricultural investment in land to changes in economic return.  Eliasp1 and eliasp2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elinag1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of agricultural investment to profit.  Elinag1 and elinag2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elinag2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of agricultural investment to changes in profit.  Elinag1 and elinag2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: enconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy demand convergence time to predicted values, in years.  Very often initial data values for countries, such as energy demand in this case, will differ a little or much from values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship or other relationship used in the model.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

nodes.NAME: endemm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy demand multiplier.  A multiplier on energy demand, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase demand and lower values decrease it.

nodes.NAME: engel
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Engel elasticities in the LES system for personal consumption, impacting terms of trade and regional development. Values above 1 cause personal consumption demand within a sector to outpace total consumption growth, and vice versa for values below 1.

nodes.NAME: eninvm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy investment multiplier.  A multiplier on energy investment, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase investment and lower values decrease it.

nodes.NAME: enon
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy switch.  This switch turns on or off the linkages between the energy submodel and all others, including economics.  When off, the economic model relies upon the simpler structure of its own energy sector.  The switch enon takes values only of 1 (on) and 0 (off).  It is often useful to disconnect submodels while exploring the behavior of any one.  The normal value is 1.

nodes.NAME: enpm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy production multiplier.  A multiplier on all types of energy production, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase production and lower values decrease it.  Warning: no cost to increased production; see ENINVM and ENINVTM for parameters to shift investment and production with trade-offs.

nodes.NAME: enprix
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy price in dollars per barrel of oil equivalent, by region.  Energy price (ENPRI) is normally computed endogenously so as to balance supply and demand of energy.  If you set enprix to positive, nonzero values, you can override the endogenous computation with your own price level.  It is possible to intervene with energy prices only for select years by leaving enprix at zero for other years and specifying enprix only for selected ones.  You might do this, for instance, to represent a period in which government controls energy prices domestically or a cartel sets them internationally.

nodes.NAME: xfdistockr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Foreign Direct Investment Stock, Annual Growth Rate.

nodes.NAME: mfpgovcor
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Government Corruption contribution to MFP.

nodes.NAME: mfpinfrel
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is currently inactive.

nodes.NAME: mfpinfrrd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is currently inactive.

nodes.NAME: mfpinfrnt
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter is currently inactive.

nodes.NAME: TAXRA
nodes.Parameter Explanation: The tax rate.  This is no longer a parameter in IFs, but rather a variable computed in the first year.  For parameter control of taxes, see taxram.

nodes.NAME: elgexpdebt1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of government revenues to government debt levels.  Elprst1 and elprst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: elgexpdebt2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of government revenues to changed in government debt levels.  Elprst1 and elprst2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: mortconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the convergence time of mortality to its expected value.  Very often initial data values for countries will differ a little or much from values predicted by a cross-sectional relationship.  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or factors idiosyncratic to countries.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country-specific "shift" should disappear. A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.

nodes.NAME: mortm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on mortality or death, by region and type. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase mortality and lower values decrease it.  Users would introduce an epidemic (like AIDS) by substantially increasing the value.  Scientific advance that greatly increased our age spans could be introduced by a value of 0.5 that is normally phased in.

nodes.NAME: lintr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Interest rate on international loans/indebtedness, expressed in the form of a ratio. For example, setting this parameter to 0.10 represents an interest rate of 10%.

nodes.NAME: lke
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Lifetime of energy capital, years.  You will normally only change this value slowly over time, maintaining the initial value.

nodes.NAME: xportr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Basic Growth Rate on International Portfolio Investment, Inward Stocks.

nodes.NAME: xwbloanr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World Bank Loan Portfolio, Basic Annual Growth Rate.

nodes.NAME: ximfcreditr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Percentage of new Credits open each year.

nodes.NAME: glocom
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Global community multiplier.  This global (not regional) parameter affects the probability of war  between any two geographic actors.   A value of 1 leaves the base probability unchanged.  A value of 1.5 would increase "community" by 50 percent and thereby decrease the probability of war by 50 percent.  A value of 0.5 would suggest a deterioration in global community.

nodes.NAME: nwarsv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Nuclear war severity factor.  This coefficient determines what portion of the nuclear armament potential will be used when a war erupts.  Values should range from 0 (none) to 1 (all).

nodes.NAME: ofscth
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Total global ocean fish catch in million metric tons. This value is set exogenously and is typically not altered from the initial setting, except for future value changes.

nodes.NAME: QE(Oil)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Capital output ratio for energy, in dollars, per barrel of production capacity, by region and energy category.  This variable determines how many dollars of capital are required in the production of a barrel of oil equivalent in each energy category.  It therefore represents the cost of energy production.  QE is exogenous only for nuclear and renewable energy.  Values for oil, gas, and coal are computed endogenously (and depend on remaining resources) and should be examined only as indicators.  To change the cost pattern for those energy forms, use resorm and increase or decrease resources.  Values for renewable and nuclear energy can be exogenously changed, but you should maintain the initial value of the base case.  A series of gradually lower costs could represent technological progress (e.g. in the solar component of renewable).  A series of gradually higher costs could represent the impact of environmental factors (e.g. increasing costs of nuclear waste disposal).  Higher or lower values will increase or decrease investment in a particular energy category and will affect its production level.  You should be aware that investment will respond only to changes over time in QE and not to changes in the initial condition.

nodes.NAME: qem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Capital output ratio for energy multiplier.  A multiplier on all types of energy capital output, unit-less, by region.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the amount of capital required per unit of energy output and lower values decrease it. Lower this parameter gradually over time to simulate a decreased cost of an energy form (such as renewable energy) as a result of technological advance.  Raise it over time to simulate the addition to the capital cost of an energy form (say nuclear) as a result of the addition to those costs of environmental ones.

nodes.NAME: rdi
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Rate of discovery for fossil fuels, initial, billion barrels of oil equivalent.  Changes in this parameter only directly effect rates of discovery in the very first year; thereafter the rates are calculated.

nodes.NAME: tconr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter specifies the increase in time-related contraception use, expressed in percentage terms.

nodes.NAME: envpm2pt5m
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on the level of residential 2.5 air pollution.

nodes.NAME: trademax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Maximum trade as a portion of tradable production base, expressed in decimal form. A value of 0.9 means 90%. Values can exceed 1.0 because some economies export and reexport more than they produce.

nodes.NAME: ttfrr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Time-related reduction in total fertility rate (TFR), in portion per year (i.e., .01 represents 1 percent).  Although time-related, it is obviously meant to represent the affect of technological and or cultural/value-based change in fertility rates.  This parameter is global, and you will often prefer to use tfrm to introduce scenarios around fertility rates, because that parameter is country/region specific.  This parameter represents, however, the historic phenomenon of "systemic shift" in fertility rates.

nodes.NAME: gdsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government expenditure by destination.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: enxl
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy export limit, ex billion barrels of oil equivalent  functions both as a switch and a numerical value, with 0 indicating no limit and positive values setting a specific limit..  Positive values (above .001) limit exports to the value specified.  For instance, a specification for a country of 0 for the first five years, 2 for the next three, and 0 thereafter,  introduces a constrain on exports of two billion barrels per year during the sixth, seventh, and eighth years.  If placed on OPEC exports, such an export restriction would be very severe.

nodes.NAME: epra
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy price responsiveness to stock/inventory levels.  Epra and eprafs are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities), most of which normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: eprafs
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy price responsiveness to change in stock/inventory levels

nodes.NAME: mfpenpri
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of multifactor productivity to energy prices.  Values (normally negative) near 0 imply little elasticity and values near -1  imply  considerable elasticity.

nodes.NAME: mfpedspn
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Multifactor Productivity Growth to an increase in education spending as a share of GDP.

nodes.NAME: mfphlspn
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Multifactor Productivity Growth to an increase in health spending as a share of GDP.

nodes.NAME: mfpedyrs
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Multifactor Productivity Growth  to an increase in years of education for adult population.

nodes.NAME: mfplife
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Multifactor Productivity Growth to an increase in life expectancy.

nodes.NAME: mfpefree
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Economic Freedom contribution to MFP.

nodes.NAME: mfpfree
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Freedom contribution to MFP.

nodes.NAME: mfpgoveff
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of Multifactor Productivity Growth to government effectiveness.

nodes.Parameter Explanation: Initial condition for rate of annual production growth.  Computed in the preprocessor, this initial condition heavily influences growth patterns.
