nodes.NAME: ENPRR(OthRenew)
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Initial condition for rate of annual production growth.  Computed in the preprocessor, this initial condition heavily influences growth patterns.

nodes.NAME: salpha
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Sectorally-specific alpha in capital's share of value added.  This value has a general empirical base and users will not normally change it.

nodes.NAME: wpcontiguity
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, response of dispute threat to geographic contiguity/proximity.  The value is in percent probability of a dispute.  That is, 3.0 would indicate that being neighbors would increase the probability of a dispute between two states by 3.0%, all else being equal.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted from other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

nodes.NAME: cpowldcf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convention power factor representing less developed country (LDC) advantage in converting military expenditures to power ("bang for the buck").  Because of lower cost structures (as often represented by higher ratios in LDCs of GDP at purchasing power parity to  GDP at exchange rates) the same levels of military expenditures may provide greater contributions to conventional military power.  This parameter specifies the maximum relative advantage for the poorest LDCs (for instance, 2 equals twice as much power added for every dollar spent).  This parameter should probably be replaced by the typical ratio of GDP at purchasing power parity to GDP at exchange rates for a given GDP per capita.

nodes.NAME: cultshseload
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Cultural region shift on survival/self-expression load.  This parameter is computed and used in the "pre-processor" of the model. Therefore changes by the user will have no effect on the model.

nodes.NAME: lifexpmin
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter determines the minimum life expectancy for PQLI calculation, expressed in years. Users will normally not change this parameter.

nodes.NAME: forestm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on forest area, by region, expressed without units. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase forest area and lower values decrease it.

nodes.NAME: fpricr1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of food prices (crops) to stock level. Frpricr1 and fpricr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters, most of which normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: fpricr2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of food prices (crops) to changes in stock level. Frpricr1 and fpricr2 are a pair of adjustment parameters, most of which normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: econfreem
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on economic freedom, expressed without units and by region. A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: encartpp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy cartel price premium.  This is a parameter (normally 0) that indicates the number of dollars/barrel that an energy cartel could add to global energy prices.  Normally a scenario using this parameter would introduced it for a specific period (e.g., 2020-2025) to represent a tight energy market allowing such a cartel to be effective, at least for a time.

nodes.NAME: keqshr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Share of capital equipment (K) in fixed capital.

nodes.NAME: meatmax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Maximum meat consumption per person, expressed in tons per person per year   limits meat consumption calculations for the initial year, in case of unreasonable data. If you wish to introduce scenarios around dietary patterns (for instance, to reduce meat consumption), use the parameter calmeatm.

nodes.NAME: nsdiv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: North-South dividing line, GDP per capita.  This parameter is only used in computing summary measures of the north-south gap in absolute or relative terms.

nodes.NAME: edtergradtrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve 100% graduation rate in tertiary education.

nodes.NAME: edterinttrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal intake rate in tertiary education.

nodes.NAME: taxinfadjm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on tax rate adjustments because of the extent of informal economy. A value of 0 specifies no adjustment; while a value of 1 specifies full adjustment.

nodes.NAME: edpriintntrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter for the number of years taken to achieve universal net intake rate in primary education.

nodes.NAME: fprihw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Historic (inertial delay) change in food prices. Values close to 1 imply very rapid adjustment and values near 0 imply little or no adjustment.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: fprimt1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of food prices (meat) to stock level. Fprimt1 and fprimt2 are a pair of adjustment parameters, most of which normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: fprimt2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of food prices (meat) to changes in stock level. Fprimt1 and fprimt2 are a pair of adjustment parameters, most of which normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: democwvmax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that determines the maximum amplitude in Polity scale points for democracy wave.  Because the Polity democracy scale runs from 1-10 (10=most democratic), it would be highly improbable that the amplitude of any wave be more than 5-6 points.

nodes.NAME: cultshts
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Cultural shift on the traditional/rational-secular index.  It is an additive factor that represents the average "shift" in the index for traditional/rational-secular for a given cultural region (relative to what would be expected based of level of GDP per capita), as identified in the World Value Survey project.  The initial value is determined from data, but the user could change the value over time to represent cultural convergence or divergence.

nodes.NAME: waron
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A switch that can be used to turn on or off the possibility of war.  A value of 0 turns off war and a value of 1 makes it possible.  It does not, however, make war certain - that will depend on calculations within each dyad of the probability of war and the conversion (via random processes) of such probabilities into actual conventional or nuclear war.

nodes.NAME: vehfuncsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Vehicle function switch.  The switch controls which of several functions the model uses to compute car and truck sales.  The standard value for it is 4, which results in the use of a function for sales per capita dependent on GDP per capita at purchasing power, the WVS index for survival/self-expression values, and the WVS index for traditional/secular-rational values.

nodes.NAME: matpostradd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive factor to introduce a shift in Materialism/post-materialism index for a region/country.  It increases or decreases the index value that the model calculates.  The normal value is zero.  See also and contrast with cultshmp, which is a cultural shift for the large cultural regions identified in the WVS project and which is calculated from data.

nodes.NAME: femshrgr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Annual growth rate of the female share in the labor force, expressed in percentage terms.

nodes.NAME: wmigrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World migration rate multiplier.  This is a very useful parameter for increasing or decreasing migration rates globally, because it applies to all rates rather than just to those for a particular country or region (for control by country/region see migrater).  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying variable and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: nwarf
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Nuclear war factor.  This is a reactivity parameter that relates the severity of a conventional war to the probability that nuclear war will erupt between acting and reacting alliances.  A value of 0 eliminates the possibility of nuclear war; a value of 1 creates a probability of war equal to the severity of conventional war (see cwarf).  By setting the value equal to 100 or more you can force the model to generate a war whenever a conventional war erupts.

nodes.NAME: wpdemmin
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, response of dispute threat to minimum democracy level in dyad.  The value is in percent probability of a dispute and is applied to the democracy level in the less democratic state in a dyad.  That is, -0.01 would indicate that every point of additional democracy on the underlying Polity scale would reduce the probability of a dispute between two states by 0.01%, all else being equal.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted from other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

nodes.NAME: wppowtran1
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, ratio of power where transition begins.  If the value were 0.7 it would indicate that when the weaker power in a dyad reached 0.7 (or 70%) of the power of the stronger, a power transition would begin.

nodes.NAME: hdilifemax

nodes.NAME: hivmdcm

nodes.NAME: mhwag
nodes.Parameter Explanation: iMport propensity, historical (inertial) delay in change.  Values near 1.0 imply very rapid adjustment and values near 0 imply little or no adjustment.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: edprisurtrgtyr

nodes.NAME: edseclowrtrantrgtyr

nodes.NAME: edsecupprtrantrgtyr

nodes.NAME: edseclowrgratrgtyr

nodes.NAME: edsecupprgratrgtyr

nodes.NAME: mfpadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive factor on Multifactor Productivity Growth.  This parameter is a powerful mechanism by which the user can increase or decrease the growth rate of countries around assumptions of the rate of productivity growth.  Normally values would be 0.0.  A value of 0.01 would introduce an added productivity growth of 1.0% annually.

nodes.NAME: mfpconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Convergence of Multifactor Productivity Growth represents the time (in years) for productivity to converge to the global function.

nodes.NAME: termtrm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on terms of trade.  The default value of this parameter is 1.0, signifying no exogenous shift in the terms of trade between more and less economically developed countries.  Relative prices in various sectors, particularly agriculture and energy, will still change endogenously.  A value greater than 1.0 additionally improves terms of trade for LDCs at the expense of developed countries.  A value of less than 1.0 shifts terms of trade to the benefit of wealthier countries.  A value of 1.2 would improve the terms of trade of the very least developed countries by about 20 percent.  This parameter should not normally be changed from 1 in the initial year.  Values should generally range from .5 to 1.5.

nodes.NAME: ylmax
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Maximum yield, by region specifies  the maximum crop yield per hectare (in metric tons) that a region can ever expect to attain in agriculture.

nodes.NAME: cultshtsload

nodes.NAME: infraelecaccruralcostm

nodes.NAME: AQUACUL

nodes.NAME: hivtadvr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Parameter that specifies the HIV technical advance rate to control spread of infection. This reflects simulation of social and behavioral change.

nodes.NAME: hivm

nodes.NAME: AIDSDRATE
nodes.Parameter Explanation: AIDS death rate as % of HIV infection rate.  This refers to the percentage of infected individuals in a population who die in a given year, not to the percentage who ultimately die of AIDS.

nodes.NAME: hivincr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Annual increase in the HIV infection rate during historic period, expressed in percentage terms. A value of 8 means an annual increase rate of 8% and these values are only used in the period prior to 2000.

nodes.NAME: wpgreatlev
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, systemic power share required for full great power status.  The value is in percent of systemic power.  Thus 5.0 would indicate that a state reached the status of full great power when its share of total global power reached 5.0%.  See also the threshold for beginning to be a great power, wpgreatlev.

nodes.NAME: wpthrconv
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, convergence time to predicted underlying threat levels.  Very often initial data values for countries, such as dyadic conflict in this case, will differ a little or much from values predicted by broader empirical analysis across states (and possibly across time).  It is never certain whether such differences involve data errors or idiosyncratic factors.  A paradigmatic assumption of IFs is that, over time, values for such variables will very often gradually converge to the values predicted by the function and the initial country- or dyad-specific "shift" should disappear.  A high value such as 10000 will effectively turn off the convergence process altogether, while a low value such as 10 will make it very rapid.  It is possible to set this parameter to 1, thereby replacing the empirical value by predicted values already in the first year and then every year thereafter.

nodes.NAME: gdsedm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on government expenditure on education by level.  A value of 1 implies no change, while higher values proportionately increase the underlying value and lower values decrease it.  Like other multipliers, user should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: terdispute
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Territorial dispute or absence (1=dispute; 0=no dispute).  This is a dyadic value, between two countries or regions.  The user could change it from 1 to 0 at some point in time to indicate the resolution of dispute.  The initial values reflect actual disputes in the early 21st century.

nodes.NAME: wpterdisp
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, increase in militarized dispute probability with territorial dispute. The value is in percent. Thus 5.0 would indicate that the probability of a dispute between two states would rise by 5.0% if they have a territorial dispute outstanding, relative to the same pair without such a dispute.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted from other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

nodes.NAME: wppowtran2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: World politics, increase in dispute probability with 10% greater power parity.  The value is in percent. Thus 0.05 would indicate that the probability of a dispute between two states would rise by 0.05% for each 10% reduction in the power differential between them (or a reduction of 0.1 on a ratio scale).  See also the threshold for the beginning of a power transition, wppowtran1.  Note that this results in a value added to or subtracted from other terms in the calculation of dispute probability (it is not used multiplicatively so as to change an otherwise calculated probability by x%).

Significant changes in the value from specification in the base case could lead to difficulties or instability in market clearing (balancing of supply and demand).

nodes.NAME: aglosstransm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on agricultural transfer/distriction losses adjusts the proportion of food transfer lost at the point of transfer.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: aglossprodm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on agricultural production losses adjusts the proportion of food production lost at the point of production (for example, to pests in the field.  Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: aglossconsm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on agricultural consumption losses adjusts the proportion of food consumption lost at the point of consumption. nodes.NAME: fishcatchm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on fish catch (freshwater and marine) unit-less, by region. Like other multipliers, you should generally not change the value in the initial year because that would override empirical initial conditions; rather you should ramp up or down the multiplier value over time.

nodes.NAME: samtomalnchpsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch to activate linkage between SAM and Malnutrition. A value of 1 indicates on, setting averted SAM cases to malnourished (instead of fully healthy).

nodes.NAME: lvherdm
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier on livestock herd.

nodes.NAME: gdscnstsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Government expenditures by destination  switch to keep constant.  A value of 1 implies switch is on, meaning GDS%GDP should be kept constant over time.

nodes.NAME: ginidomcnstsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Domestic Gini Index constant switch.  Values of 0 turn off and allow endogenous computation; 1 starts the consant period with the last saved value.

nodes.NAME: enpadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy production additive factor.  An additve factor on all types of energy production, unit-less, by region.  A value of 0 implies no change, while positive values proportionately increase production and negative values decrease it.  Warning: no cost to increased production; see ENINVM and ENINVTM for parameters to shift investment and production with trade-offs.

nodes.NAME: eninvadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Energy investment additive factor.  An additive factor on energy investment, in Billion $, by region.  A value of 0 implies no change, while positive values increase investment and negative values decrease it.

nodes.NAME: edprienrm

nodes.NAME: edseclowrenrm

nodes.NAME: edprienrgrdm

nodes.NAME: edseclowrenrgrdm

nodes.NAME: ennoprodsw

nodes.NAME: sfintlwaralltoginidom
nodes.Parameter Explanation: This parameter serves as a multiplier that adjusts the Gini coefficient based on the probability of conflict. However, the actual increase is adjusted by the probability of conflict; thus, with a 50% probability of conflict, the Gini coefficient would only increase by 1%.

nodes.NAME: waterhhsafetrgtyr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Water Services, Safely Managed, years from model base year to reach the target value stored in the parameter waterhhsafetrgtval. The year count starts from the initial year of the mdoel.

nodes.NAME: sanithhmodel2sw

nodes.NAME: democpolyarchym

nodes.NAME: democpolyarchyadd
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Additive factor to the Polyarchy Index.

nodes.NAME: ksm

nodes.NAME: sfcivilwarucdpsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: State failure/internal war UCDP switch .   When the swithc is 1 the variable SFCIVILWARUCDP will be connected to forward linkagess and parameters, otherwise variable SFINTLWARALL will be used.

nodes.NAME: qevremul
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Multiplier to impact the VRE cost increase as VRE share goes above threshold. A value of 1 means no impact. Values above 1 means cost increase. Values below 1 means decrease.

nodes.NAME: qevrethr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: A parameter to set the percentage share of VRE in total energy use at which VRE costs (QE) starts to increase.

nodes.NAME: elcaput1

nodes.NAME: elcaput2
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Elasticity of capacity utilization to stock level change.  Elcaput1 and elcaput2 are a pair of adjustment parameters (not true elasticities) that normally have about a 1:2 ratio.  Significant changes in this parameter could destabilize model behavior.

nodes.NAME: migminpoplimit
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Once Population reaches this portion of initial population migration out stops

nodes.NAME: migrateoutr
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Outward migration of a population in percent per year.  Because global emigration and immigration must balance, changes in this value for a single country/region may not change migration/population as substantially as the change introduced originally.

nodes.NAME: migrateinr

Because global emigration and immigration must balance, changes in this value for a single country/region may not change migration/population as substantially as the change introduced in migrater.

nodes.NAME: mcadjsw
nodes.Parameter Explanation: Switch for import capacity adjustment. When the switch is ON, we adjust Imports based on changes in exports from main partners.

nodes.NAME: wpsovcount
